The password must meet minimum complexity requirements to ensure account security. Upon successful registration, the seller account is inserted into the ecommerce_mall_sellers table with the hashed password and pending_approval status.

After registration, the seller receives initial authentication tokens that allow them to access their account dashboard and view their approval status. However, the seller cannot list products, manage inventory, or process orders until their account receives administrator approval. The seller can track their registration status through the approval workflow.

If the email address is already registered, the operation fails with a conflict error. If the email format is invalid, the operation fails with a validation error. If the password does not meet complexity requirements, the operation fails with a validation error. The access token grants temporary access to seller operations, while the refresh token allows obtaining new access tokens without re-authenticating. The seller receives these tokens along with their account information.

If the email address is not found in the system, the login fails with a not found error. If the password is incorrect, the login fails with an authentication error. If the account has been banned or rejected by an administrator, the login is denied. Successful login provides the seller with full platform access appropriate to their approval status.

The seller receives the new token pair which grants continued access to seller operations.

The refresh operation is designed to maintain seamless user experience by allowing tokens to be renewed before expiration. Sellers should implement automatic token refresh logic in their client applications to avoid authentication interruptions during prolonged usage. The refresh token has a longer validity period than the access token to reduce the frequency of re-authentication.

If the refresh token is invalid, expired, or has already been used, the operation fails. If the seller account has been banned or deleted since the token was issued, the refresh fails. The seller will need to perform a full login operation to obtain new credentials.

Upon successful validation, new session records are created in ecommerce_mall_super_admin_sessions table with access tokens and refresh tokens.

For security, the system invalidates any existing active sessions for the super administrator before issuing new tokens, ensuring single session policy or enabling session revocation capability. Successful authentication is logged in the activity tracking system for audit purposes.

Token expiry times are strictly enforced based on the configured session duration in the platform configuration. Access tokens have shorter lifespans (e.g., 15 minutes) for reduced exposure, while refresh tokens have longer lifespans (e.g., 7 days) for convenience. The refresh token response includes the new access token and refresh token with their respective expiration timestamps.

Security: Only the profile owner (authenticated customer) can update their own profile. Customer profiles are private and cannot be viewed or modified by other users.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of product categories for browsing and discovery.

This operation returns categories organized hierarchically from the `ecommerce_mall_categories` table, supporting filtering by `is_active` status, `parent_id` for hierarchical navigation, `display_order` for ranking, and search terms in the `name` or `slug` columns. Categories serve as the organizational structure that customers use to browse and discover products in the e-commerce platform.

Supports pagination with configurable page size and cursor-based navigation for efficient browsing of large category lists. Results are sorted by `display_order` by default (ascending) to show primary categories first, with additional sorting options for `name` (alphabetical) or `created_at` (newest first).

All registered actors (customers, sellers, administrators, super administrators) can browse categories. Categories with `is_active=false` are excluded from results by default but can be included for administrative purposes. Soft-deleted categories (where `deleted_at` is not null) are always excluded from customer browsing but may be included for administrative audit purposes.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_categories table with pagination and filtering.

Apply search filters:
- Search by name (partial match) or slug (exact match) from IRequest.searchTerm
- Filter by parent_id for hierarchical browsing (retrieve subcategories of a specific parent)
- Filter by is_active status to include only active categories
- Sort by display_order (ascending), name (alphabetical), or created_at (newest first)

Pagination:
- Use cursor-based pagination with pagination.page and pagination.pageSize
- Return hasNextPage and cursor for next page navigation

Hierarchy:
- Return parent_id and children count for each category to enable tree navigation
- For categories with parent_id, include parent category summary for breadcrumb display

Security:
- Validate actor authentication
- If includesDeleted=true and actor is not admin, return only active categories
- If includesDeleted=true and actor is admin, include soft-deleted categories where deleted_at is not null

Edge cases:
- Root categories (parent_id=null) have no parent category reference
- Leaf categories (no children) return empty children array
- Handle concurrent category modifications with appropriate locking

Categories are the primary classification mechanism for organizing products on the platform. Each category contains metadata used for display in navigation menus, category listing pages, and product filtering interfaces. The active status determines whether the category is visible to customers browsing the catalog.

Both customers and administrators can retrieve category details. Customers use this endpoint to view category information before browsing products, while administrators use it to manage category content. The operation validates that the category exists and returns a 404 error if the category ID is not found.

Administrators specify the category identifier and provide the new name and/or description values in the request body. The updated category information becomes immediately visible to customers browsing the category list and product catalog.

The category hierarchy remains unchanged during an update operation. Only the category's name and description fields are modifiable. Parent-child relationships cannot be altered through this endpoint.

Related Operations:
- GET /categories/{categoryId} must be called to retrieve the current category details before editing
- PATCH /categories can be used to browse and search all categories

operations.description:
Retrieve all historical snapshots for a specific category, showing how the category information has changed over time.

This operation provides a complete audit trail of all modifications made to a category, including changes to the category name, description, slug, parent relationship, display order, active status, and other metadata. Each snapshot represents the category's state at a specific point in time when an edit occurred.

Administrators can use this endpoint to track category evolution, investigate when specific changes were made, and review historical category structures for dispute resolution or compliance purposes. The response includes paginated results optimized for displaying snapshot lists, with each snapshot containing the captured state at the time of creation.

The endpoint requires administrator access as it provides historical audit data. Customers cannot access this endpoint. The operation filters snapshots by the provided category ID and supports pagination, sorting, and optional date range filtering to manage large result sets efficiently.
operations.name: index

Query ecommerce_mall_category_snapshots table filtered by snapshot_id = categoryId.

   - WHERE clause: snapshot_id = {categoryId}
   - ORDER BY: created_at DESC for most recent first
   - Pagination parameters: page, pageSize (default page=1, pageSize=20)
   - Optional filters: date range (created_at BETWEEN), snapshot type
4. Return paginated results with total count for pagination metadata
5. Each snapshot row includes all captured fields at snapshot creation time

Handle edge cases:
- Category exists but has no snapshots (return empty list)
- Category does not exist (return 404 error)
- Invalid UUID format (return 400 error)
- Non-administrator access (return 403 error)

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of products from the ecommerce mall product catalog.

This operation provides comprehensive search and filtering capabilities for browsing products. Customers can discover products across all sellers, while sellers can view and manage their own product listings. The operation supports multiple filter criteria including category, product status, seller, and name search.

Supports advanced pagination with configurable page size and cursor-based navigation for efficient large result set handling. Results can be sorted by various fields including product name, creation date, update date, and base price. The response includes product summary information optimized for display in product listing pages.

Each product returned includes essential information such as product ID, name, base price, category, status, and image reference. Full product details should be retrieved using the GET /products/{productId} endpoint for individual product viewing.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_products table with pagination, filtering, and sorting.

Apply search filters:
- category_id: Filter by product category (exact match)
- status: Filter by product status (active, inactive, out_of_stock)
- seller_id: Filter by owner seller (required for sellers viewing own products, optional for customers viewing all)
- name: Partial name search using trigram index for fuzzy matching
- base_price: Range filter (min, max)

Apply sorting:
- sort_by: Field to sort by (name, created_at, updated_at, base_price, display_order)
- sort_order: Direction (asc, desc)

Apply pagination:
- page: Page number (1-based)
- pageSize: Number of items per page (10-100, default 20)

Return cursor-based pagination for large result sets with next/previous cursor support.

For customer users (customer actor): Return all active products across all sellers, excluding deleted products.
For seller users (seller actor): Return products owned by the authenticated seller, with optional filtering to view specific product status.
Exclude soft-deleted products (deleted_at IS NULL) from results.

Join with ecommerce_mall_categories for category information when needed.
Join with ecommerce_mall_product_images for primary thumbnail image when included in response projection.

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information for a specific product in the ecommerce_mall product catalog.

This operation returns complete product details including the product name, description, base price, and category classification. The response includes the owning seller's information, product status (active/inactive/out_of_stock), and all associated product images with their display order.

Security and Access Control:
Products are visible to authenticated customers when owned by active seller accounts (seller.deleted_at is null). The product status field indicates whether the item is currently available for purchase. Products from sellers that have been soft-deleted (deleted_at is set) are not visible in customer-facing listings.

Product Variants and Images:
Each product may have multiple variants (ecommerce_mall_product_variants) representing different option combinations such as size, color, or capacity. The product also supports multiple images (ecommerce_mall_product_images) with the first image by display_order serving as the main thumbnail for catalog displays.

Business Context:
Products form the core inventory of the marketplace, belonging to exactly one seller (the product owner) and classified under a single category for customer browsing. Historical product state changes are preserved through snapshots (ecommerce_mall_product_snapshots) for audit trails and dispute resolution.

Related Operations:
Use PATCH /products with IRequest body to search and filter products by category, price range, or seller. Use GET /categories/{categoryId} to browse products by category. View seller details using GET /sellers/{sellerId} to see the shop owner information.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_products table using productId as UUID primary key.

1. Load product by id where deleted_at is null (exclude soft-deleted products)
2. Join ecommerce_mall_sellers to get seller shop name and status
3. Join ecommerce_mall_categories to get category name and hierarchy
4. Load product images ordered by display_order ascending
5. Load product variants with inventory status
6. Verify seller account is not suspended or rejected (hide if so per 01-actors-and-auth.md)
7. Return full product detail with nested seller and category data

Error handling:
- Return 404 if productId not found or product is soft-deleted
- Return 404 if product belongs to suspended/rejected seller (invisible products)
- Validate productId format is valid UUID

responseBody.description: Detailed product information including seller and category data

parameters.name: productId

operations.description:
Create a new product for the seller's catalog in the e-commerce marketplace.

This operation allows registered sellers to add new products to their shop's product catalog. The product must include a display name, detailed description, category classification, and base price. Products serve as the core inventory items that customers can browse and purchase.

Each product requires a unique slug for SEO-friendly URLs, which is automatically generated from the product name but can be customized. The product status defaults to 'active' when created, making it immediately visible in customer browsing and search results.

Products belong exclusively to the creating seller and can only be managed by that seller. Every product edit creates a snapshot for audit trail purposes. Products cannot be deleted if they have associated order items, cancellation requests, or refund requests.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new product record in the ecommerce_mall_products table.

1. Extract seller_id from the authenticated seller's session context (do not allow manual specification)
2. Validate that name is provided and non-empty
3. Validate that description is provided and non-empty
4. Validate that category_id references an existing active category
5. Validate that base_price is positive
6. Generate slug from name if not provided, or use provided slug if unique
7. Set status to 'active' by default
8. Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp
9. Insert the product record into ecommerce_mall_products
10. Return the complete product record with all fields populated

Error handling:
- 400 if name, description, category_id, or base_price is missing/invalid
- 400 if slug already exists
- 401 if seller is not authenticated
- 404 if category_id does not reference an existing category

Note: Products without variants will be created but marked as unavailable for purchase. Sellers should create at least one variant after product creation.

responseBody.description: Created product with all details including id, timestamps, and seller information

requestBody.description: Product creation data including name, description, category, base price, and optional slug

operations.description:
Update an existing product's details. This operation allows the product owner (seller) to modify product attributes including name, description, base price, status, and slug. Every update operation automatically creates a snapshot to preserve the previous state for audit trails and dispute resolution.

The product must belong to the authenticated seller making the update request. Cross-ownership updates are not permitted - sellers can only modify products they own.

This operation supports partial updates by including only the fields that need to be changed. Any fields omitted from the request body will retain their current values. The updated product immediately reflects in search results and category listings.

Product status changes (active, inactive, out_of_stock) affect product visibility to customers. Status transitions are validated against business rules regarding variant inventory and orders.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Validate productId exists and is valid UUID format
2. Fetch product record from ecommerce_mall_products table
3. Verify ownership: authenticated seller_id must match product.seller_id
4. Create snapshot of current product state before applying changes
5. Update only provided fields in request body:
   - name: String, required validation for non-empty
   - description: String?, nullable
   - base_price: Float, must be positive
   - slug: String, must be unique across platform
   - status: String, must be one of: 'active', 'inactive', 'out_of_stock'
6. Validate no variants have pending order items, cancellation requests, or refund requests (if deleting variants)
7. Apply UPDATE query with new values and updated_at timestamp
8. Return complete updated product entity with all relationships

Error handling:
- 404 if product not found
- 403 if seller does not own the product
- 400 if validation fails (empty name, invalid status, duplicate slug)
- 400 if product cannot be modified due to pending orders/requests

responseBody.description: The updated product entity with all fields and relationships.

parameters.description: The UUID of the product to update.
parameters.name: productId

requestBody.description: Partial update fields for the product. Only include fields that need to be changed.

prerequisites.description: Product must be created before it can be updated. PUT operation requires the product to exist in the system.

operations.description:
Soft delete a product from the marketplace, removing it from active product listings while preserving historical data.

This operation marks the specified product as deleted using soft deletion, removing it from the platform's active product catalog without permanently erasing the data. The product will no longer appear in search results, category listings, or any customer-facing product browsing interfaces.

Before deletion succeeds, the system validates that the product meets all deletion criteria:
- The requesting user must own the product (if a seller) or have administrator privileges
- No variants of the product may have order items with paid or shipped status
- No variants may have pending cancellation requests
- No variants may have pending refund requests

When validation passes, the operation performs soft deletion:
- The Product record is marked as deleted by setting the deleted_at timestamp
- The product is removed from active listings and search results
- Product snapshots are preserved permanently for dispute resolution, audit trails, and historical reference
- The product's deletion is logged for compliance tracking

Important: Soft deletion preserves the product data in the database for legal and business requirements. The product can be referenced in existing orders through its snapshot data even though it no longer appears in the active catalog.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Validate authentication and extract user identity and role
2. Query ecommerce_mall_products table for the product by productId (UUID)
3. If not found, return 404 Not Found
4. Validate ownership/authorization:
   - If user is a seller: verify product.ownerId equals user's seller ID
   - If user is admin/superAdmin: allow deletion
   - Otherwise return 403 Forbidden
5. Check deletion constraints (must all pass):
   - Query ecommerce_mall_product_variants for any variant where productId = target and that has orderItems with status IN ('paid', 'shipped')
   - Query ecommerce_mall_product_variants for any variant that has cancellationRequests with status != 'completed' and status != 'rejected'
   - Query ecommerce_mall_product_variants for any variant that has refundRequests with status != 'completed' and status != 'rejected'
   - If any constraint fails, return 409 Conflict with error message
6. Begin database transaction
7. Delete all InventoryRecord records where productVariant.id is in the set of variant IDs
8. Delete all ProductVariant records where productId = target
9. Delete the Product record
10. Commit transaction
11. Return 200 OK with deleted product data (name, category, basePrice, and variant count)
12. Log deletion event for compliance tracking

parameters.description: UUID of the product to be deleted from the marketplace
parameters.name: productId

prerequisites.description: Product must be created before it can be deleted from the marketplace catalog

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of product variants belonging to a specific product.

This operation allows sellers to view all variants belonging to their product with comprehensive search and filtering capabilities. Each variant represents a unique combination of product options (such as size, color, material) with a unique SKU code, individual pricing, and stock quantity tracking.

**Authorization Requirements**

This operation requires seller authentication. Sellers can only access variants for products they own—the system validates that the authenticated seller's ID matches the product's seller_id before returning any variant data. Attempting to access another seller's products will result in an authorization error.

**Search and Filtering**

Supports filtering by stock quantity ranges, variant status (active, inactive, or discontinued values defined in the database), price ranges using base_price or sale_price fields, and SKU code patterns using trigram search for fuzzy matching. Results are sorted by sort_order with pagination for efficient browsing of large variant sets.

**Response Content**

Each variant response includes complete option key-value pairs aggregated from the ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options child table, along with base price, optional sale price, current stock quantity, reserved quantity, and status information. Soft-deleted variants (where deleted_at is not null) are excluded from results.

**Pagination and Ordering**

Results support configurable page size, sort field selection, and sort direction. The default sort is by sort_order ascending with created_at descending as a secondary sort for consistent ordering.

Related operations:
- GET /ecommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants/{variantId} - Retrieve a single variant
- POST /ecommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants - Create a new variant
- PUT /ecommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants/{variantId} - Update a variant
- DELETE /ecommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}/variants/{variantId} - Soft delete a variant
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_product_variants table where product_id matches the path parameter productId.

Validate that the requesting seller owns the product by checking ecommerce_mall_products.seller_id against the authenticated seller's ID.

Apply search filters from request body:
- stock_quantity: range filter (min, max)
- status: enum filter (active, inactive, discontinued)
- base_price: numeric range filter
- sku: pattern match using gin_trgm_ops trigram search
- is_default: boolean filter

Join with ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options to aggregate option key-value pairs as JSON object.

Apply pagination parameters: page number, page size, sort field, sort direction.

Return cursor-based pagination metadata for next/previous page navigation.

Sort variants by sort_order ascending by default, with secondary sort by created_at descending.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of product variant summaries with complete option details

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the product whose variants to retrieve
parameters.name: productId

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering product variants

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific product variant within a product.

This operation returns complete variant information including the SKU code, option values (such as color, size, material), price (which may override the product base price), and current stock quantity. The variant must belong to the specified product, and both the product and variant must exist in the system.

The variant price displays its specific value if it differs from the product's base price, or shows the base price if no override was set. Option values are displayed as key-value pairs representing the variant's characteristics (e.g., {"color": "Red", "size": "Large"}).

Customers can view unavailable variants (out of stock or product without variants), but these cannot be added to the shopping cart. Sellers can view all their product variants including those with pending orders or cancellation/refund requests, which restricts variant deletion.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_product_variants table for the specific variant identified by variantId parameter. Verify that the variant belongs to the product identified by productId parameter by checking the product_variant_id foreign key relationship.

Fetch the variant's complete record including: id, sku, product_id, price (nullable), stock_quantity, and timestamps (created_at, updated_at).

Query the ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options table to retrieve all option key-value pairs for this variant (e.g., color, size, material options).

Return the complete variant object with options joined. If variant or product does not exist, return 404 Not Found.

If the variant's price is null, indicate that the variant uses the product's base price. Calculate the stock status based on current stock_quantity (available if > 0, out of stock if = 0).

Access control: Allow any authenticated actor (customer, seller, admin, superAdmin) to retrieve variant details. Sellers can only access variants they own; others can view public product variants.

operations.description:
Update an existing product variant within a seller's product catalog.

This operation allows sellers to modify variant properties including the unique SKU code, option values (key-value pairs for attributes like size, color, material), pricing information (base price and optional sale price), and status. Every edit operation automatically creates an immutable snapshot capturing the variant state before modification for audit trail and dispute resolution purposes.

The variant must belong to a product owned by the authenticated seller. The SKU code must remain unique across all variants in the system. Stock quantity cannot be modified directly through this endpoint as it is managed through dedicated inventory record operations.

After successful update, the variant becomes immediately available in product listings with the new properties. The updated_at timestamp is automatically set to the current time. If the variant is a default selection for the product, changing the is_default flag affects product display ordering.

Related operations:
- GET /products/{productId}/variants - List all variants for a product
- GET /products/{productId}/variants/{variantId} - Retrieve variant details
- DELETE /products/{productId}/variants/{variantId} - Delete variant (if no pending orders)
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Authorization: Verify seller actor authentication and ownership of the parent product (product_id matches seller's product records)

2. Path Parameter Validation: Validate productId and variantId are valid UUID format

3. Record Lookup: Query ecommerce_mall_product_variants table for variantId, join with ecommerce_mall_products to verify product_id ownership

4. Update Restrictions: Stock quantity is read-only (managed through inventory_records). Reserved_quantity is system-managed.

5. SKU Uniqueness Check: Verify sku field uniqueness across all product_variants in ecommerce_mall_product_variants.sku (unique constraint)

6. Options Format Validation: Ensure options field contains valid JSON object with string key-value pairs. Consider migrating to ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options child table.

7. Price Validation: base_price must be non-negative number. sale_price must be either null or positive and not exceed base_price.

8. Status Validation: Accept only valid status values (active, inactive, discontinued)

9. Snapshot Creation: Insert record into ecommerce_mall_product_variant_snapshots capturing complete variant state before modification (snapshot_type = 'update')

10. Database Update: Execute UPDATE on ecommerce_mall_product_variants setting sku, options, base_price, sale_price, status, sort_order, is_default, updated_at = NOW()

11. Response Construction: Return complete updated variant object with all fields including relationships (product reference)

12. Error Handling:
    - 404: Variant not found or does not belong to seller's product
    - 400: Invalid SKU (duplicate), invalid options format, invalid price values, invalid status value
    - 403: Seller does not own the product

13. Transaction: All operations (snapshot, update) must be atomic within a database transaction

operations.description:
Soft delete a product variant from the seller's product catalog.

This operation marks a product variant as deleted by setting the deleted_at timestamp. The variant is removed from active product listings and will no longer appear in search results or customer-facing product detail pages.

A variant can only be deleted if it has no pending order items with paid or shipped status, no pending cancellation requests, and no pending refund requests. This restriction preserves order history integrity and prevents deletion of variants with active transactions.

The seller must own the product containing this variant. Authorization is enforced by verifying the authenticated seller's ID matches the product's seller_id field.

When a variant is soft deleted:
- The variant's deleted_at timestamp is set (variant remains in database for historical records)
- All associated inventory records are also soft deleted (their deleted_at timestamps are set)
- The variant no longer appears in active product listings or search results
- Product snapshots and historical order data remain intact and unaffected
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Execute DELETE operation on ecommerce_mall_product_variants table.

1. Validate authentication: Ensure authenticated user is a seller actor.

2. Verify ownership: Query ecommerce_mall_products to confirm the product exists and belongs to the authenticated seller (products.seller_id == authenticatedSellerId).

3. Validate deletion conditions by checking for pending transactions:
   - Query ecommerce_mall_order_items for any items referencing this variant with order status 'paid' or 'shipped'
   - Query ecommerce_mall_cancellation_requests for any pending requests for order items containing this variant
   - Query ecommerce_mall_refund_requests for any pending requests for order items containing this variant

4. If any pending transactions exist, reject deletion with error 409 (Conflict) including explanation of blocking transactions.

5. If validation passes, delete the variant record from ecommerce_mall_product_variants.

6. Delete all inventory records (ecommerce_mall_inventory_records) associated with this variant.

7. Return the deleted variant's complete data including id, skuCode, basePrice, and all option values.

8. Ensure atomicity: All deletions occur within a single transaction.

operations.description:
Update the display order and metadata for product images within a product catalog.

This operation allows sellers to reorder images in their product's image gallery by specifying new display_order values. The image with the lowest display_order value (typically 0) serves as the main product thumbnail and is displayed in product listings, search results, and promotional areas throughout the platform.

Reordering Logic:
- Images are displayed in ascending order of display_order values
- The image with the lowest display_order (0) becomes the primary thumbnail
- When an image is deleted, the system does not automatically reassign another image as thumbnail - sellers must explicitly manage this
- All display_order values must form a continuous sequence without duplicates

Ownership Requirements:
Only the seller who owns the product can modify its images. The system verifies that the requesting seller's account is associated with the product before applying any changes. Sellers can only manage images for products in their own storefront.

Related Operations:
- Use GET /ecommerceMall/seller/products/{productId} to retrieve product details before updating images
- Use DELETE /ecommerceMall/seller/products/{productId}/images/{imageId} to remove individual product images
- Use PATCH /ecommerceMall/seller/products/{productId} to update product metadata

4. Validate all provided image IDs belong to the specified product
5. Validate display_order values form a valid sequence (no duplicates)
6. Within a transaction:
   - Update display_order for each image in ecommerce_mall_product_images
   - If any image had display_order=0 and is now moved, mark the next lowest as new primary (application-level tracking)
7. Return updated product images with their new display order

**Edge Cases**:
- If productId doesn't exist: return 404 not found
- If seller doesn't own product: return 403 forbidden
- If image IDs don't belong to product: return 400 bad request
- If display_order has duplicates: return 400 bad request
- Empty request body: return 400 bad request

operations.description:
Update the option key-value pairs for a specific product variant.

This endpoint allows sellers to manage the customization options (such as size, color, material) associated with a product variant. Each option is stored as an atomic key-value pair, where the key represents the option type (e.g., 'size', 'color') and the value represents the specific choice (e.g., 'Large', 'Red').

The operation supports batch modifications through a structured request body that can add new options, update existing option values, or remove specific options. Each option key must be unique within a variant - the database enforces a composite unique constraint on (product_variant_id, key) to prevent duplicate option types.

Authorization: Only the seller who owns the parent product can update variant options. The system validates that both the product and variant exist, the variant belongs to the specified product, and neither entity is deleted.

Every option update triggers an automatic snapshot creation for audit trail and dispute resolution. Snapshots preserve the complete variant state including all option combinations at the time of modification.

Related Operations:
- GET /products/{productId}/variants/{variantId} - View complete variant details including current options
- PATCH /products/{productId}/variants/{variantId} - Update variant-level properties (price, stock, status)
- POST /products/{productId}/variants - Create a new variant with initial options
operations.name: updateOptions
operations.specification:
1. Authentication & Authorization:
   - Authenticate seller actor via JWT session token
   - Verify seller owns the product referenced by productId
   - Validate variant exists and belongs to the product
   - Ensure product and variant are not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null)

2. Input Validation:
   - Validate productId and variantId are valid UUIDs
   - Verify variant.product_id matches productId (cross-reference check)
   - Validate options array is provided and non-empty
   - Check for duplicate option keys within the request body
   - Ensure option key format is valid (non-empty string, no special characters)

3. Batch Operations Execution:
   - For each 'add' action: Insert new record into ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options
     - Ensure (product_variant_id, key) uniqueness (database constraint)
     - Set product_variant_id to variantId
     - Set key and value from request
   - For each 'update' action: Find existing record by key and update value
     - Record must belong to this variant
     - Update value field only
   - For each 'remove' action: Soft delete record by setting deleted_at
     - Find record by key belonging to this variant
     - Mark as deleted (do not permanently remove)

4. Snapshot Creation:
   - Create ecommerce_mall_product_variant_snapshot for this variant
   - Capture complete variant state including all current option values
   - Store timestamp and actor reference for audit trail
   - Preserve snapshot for dispute resolution and historical tracking

5. Database Query Pattern:
   - Use transaction for atomicity of all option operations
   - SELECT variant WHERE id = variantId AND product_id = productId AND deleted_at IS NULL
   - For adds: INSERT INTO ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options (product_variant_id, key, value, created_at, updated_at)
   - For updates: UPDATE ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options SET value = ?, updated_at = NOW() WHERE product_variant_id = ? AND key = ? AND deleted_at IS NULL
   - For removes: UPDATE ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options SET deleted_at = NOW() WHERE product_variant_id = ? AND key = ? AND deleted_at IS NULL
   - Create snapshot after successful option operations

6. Error Handling:
   - 404 Not Found: Product or variant not found, variant does not belong to product, or entity is deleted
   - 403 Forbidden: Seller does not own the product
   - 400 Bad Request: Duplicate option keys in request, invalid option key format, empty options array
   - 409 Conflict: Option key already exists for this variant (for add operations)

7. Response:
   - Return updated variant summary with all active (non-deleted) options
   - Include full variant details: id, sku, price, stock, status, options array
   - Options should be sorted by sort_order or alphabetically by key

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific product variant option by its identifier.

This operation returns the detailed information of a single option attribute for a product variant. Options are stored as key-value pairs representing customization choices such as size, color, material, pattern, or any other product-specific attributes that differentiate one variant from another within the same product catalog.

**Hierarchical Identification**

The endpoint uses a three-level hierarchy to precisely locate the desired option:
- **Product** (productId): The parent product in the catalog
- **Variant** (variantId): A specific option combination within that product
- **Option** (optionId): An individual attribute definition (e.g., size=Large, color=Red)

This hierarchical structure ensures that options are always scoped to their parent variant and product, preventing any ambiguity when multiple products may have similarly-named options.

**Option Structure**

Each option contains:
- **key**: The attribute type (e.g., 'size', 'color', 'material')
- **value**: The normalized option value (e.g., 'Large', 'Red', 'Cotton')
- **Timestamps**: Creation and last update times for audit purposes

**Use Cases**

- Customer browsing a product: View all available variant options and their values
- Seller managing inventory: Inspect option attributes when editing variants
- System processes: Validate option data integrity

**Relationship to Other Operations**

This operation is typically called after retrieving a variant's details (GET /products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}) to inspect individual option attributes. The variant endpoint may include an aggregate of options, but this operation provides full details for a single option including audit trail timestamps.

Step 3: Locate the option record identified by optionId
Step 4: Ensure the option's product_variant_id matches the variantId (cross-reference validation)
Step 5: Return the complete option record with id, product_variant_id, key, value, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at fields

Error handling:
- 404 if product does not exist
- 404 if variant does not exist or does not belong to the product
- 404 if option does not exist
- 404 if option's parent variant does not match the requested variantId

Note: The option table uses soft deletion (deleted_at nullable), so deleted options should be excluded from results.

Add a new option attribute to a specific product variant.

This operation allows a seller to create a new option (such as 'size', 'color', 'material', or a custom attribute) for a product variant they own. Each option represents a key-value pair that describes a specific characteristic of the variant.

The seller must own the parent product to add options to its variants. The system enforces a unique constraint on the combination of variant and option key, preventing duplicate option types for the same variant (e.g., you cannot add two different 'size' options to the same variant).

A snapshot of the variant option attributes is automatically created when the option is added to maintain an audit trail of option changes. The option becomes immediately available when customers view the variant's option combinations.

Related operations:
- GET /products/{productId}/variants/{variantId} - Retrieve variant details including all options
- PATCH /products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}/options/{optionId} - Update an existing option
- DELETE /products/{productId}/variants/{variantId}/options/{optionId} - Remove an option from the variant

This operation respects the seller's ownership boundary and validates that the product exists and is owned by the authenticated seller before creating the option.

4. Check that the key is not already used by another option for this variant (enforce @@unique([product_variant_id, key]) constraint)
5. Insert a new record into ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options with the provided key, value, sort_order, product_variant_id set to variantId, and auto-generated id and timestamps
6. Create an audit snapshot of the variant after adding the option (record creation event)
7. Return the newly created option object with all fields populated

Error handling:
- 404 Not Found: Product not found, variant not found, or variant does not belong to the product
- 403 Forbidden: Product is not owned by the authenticated seller
- 409 Conflict: Option key already exists for this variant
- 400 Bad Request: Missing required fields or invalid data types

- SELECT variants.id, variants.product_id WHERE variants.id = variantId AND variants.product_id = productId

operations.description:
Update an existing product variant option attribute that defines specific customization characteristics for a product variant.

This operation allows sellers to modify the key name (option type) and/or value (option value) of a variant option. For example, updating a size option from 'Large' to 'Extra Large', or changing a color option key from 'primary_color' to 'color'.

Each option belongs to exactly one product variant, and the combination of product variant and option key must remain unique. When updating an option's key, the system validates that no other option for the same variant uses the same key name.

Security: Only the seller who owns the parent product can modify variant options on that product. Authentication and seller identity verification are required.

Soft delete support: The option record can be soft deleted via the deleted_at timestamp field, preserving historical option data for audit purposes while hiding it from active product listings.

Note: Unlike product variants, individual option records do not create snapshots on update. The ecommerce_mall_product_variant_snapshots table captures variant-level state (SKU, price, stock quantity, status) but does not track individual option modifications.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Execute a PUT request to update the ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options table record.

Step 1: Authentication and Authorization
- Verify the request contains valid seller session token
- Extract seller_id from authenticated session

Step 2: Parameter Validation
- Validate productId, variantId, and optionId are valid UUIDs
- Verify product exists and is owned by the authenticated seller

- Verify option exists and belongs to the specified variant

Step 3: Request Body Validation
- At least one of 'key' or 'value' must be provided in requestBody
- If 'key' is provided, validate it doesn't conflict with existing options for the same variant
  * Query ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options for same product_variant_id with same key
  * Exclude the current optionId from the check (allowing key to remain unchanged)
  * Return 409 Conflict if duplicate key found
- Validate key and value string lengths (recommend max 50 chars for key, 100 chars for value)
- Validate key matches pattern for option attribute names (alphanumeric, underscore, hyphen)

Step 4: Database Update
- Update the option record with new key and/or value values
- Set updated_at to current timestamp
- If key is being changed, ensure unique constraint [product_variant_id, key] remains satisfied

Step 5: Snapshot Creation
- Create an entry in ecommerce_mall_product_variant_snapshots table capturing the option state before update
- Store original key, value, and relevant metadata
- Link snapshot to the updated option via option_id

Step 6: Response
- Return the updated option record with all fields including new values
- Include updated_at timestamp showing when modification occurred

Error Handling:
- 404 Not Found: If product, variant, or option doesn't exist
- 403 Forbidden: If seller doesn't own the product
- 400 Bad Request: If requestBody is invalid or missing required fields
- 409 Conflict: If new key conflicts with existing option for same variant
- 422 Unprocessable Entity: If validation constraints are violated (string lengths, patterns)

Performance Considerations:
- Use transaction to ensure atomic update + snapshot creation
- Index on product_variant_id enables fast lookup for conflict detection
- Composite unique constraint enforced at database level provides final protection

operations.description:
Remove a specific option attribute (such as size, color, or material) from a product variant.

This operation deletes an option entry from the ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options table, which stores product variant options as atomic key-value pairs. Each option represents a specific attribute type (key) with its corresponding value for a variant, such as {size: "Large"} or {color: "Red"}.

The operation requires the seller to own the parent product of the variant being modified. Authorization checks ensure sellers can only remove options from their own products, not from other sellers' products.

When an option is deleted, the variant's option set is reduced. If all options are removed from a variant, the variant may become invalid or unusable. Sellers should ensure variants retain at least one meaningful option before deletion. The option deletion does not affect existing order items that reference the variant - historical order data remains intact through snapshot references.

The variant and its parent product remain unchanged; only the specific option attribute entry is removed from the database. Related inventory records, order items, and shipment references continue to function normally.

Related operations:
- PATCH /products/{productId}/variants - List all variants for a product
- PUT /products/{productId}/variants/{variantId} - Update variant details
- POST /products/{productId}/variants - Create a new variant with options

Delete a specific option attribute from a product variant.

1. Fetch the product by productId from ecommerce_mall_products

3. Fetch the variant by variantId from ecommerce_mall_product_variants
4. Validate variant_id matches the fetched variant
5. Verify the product_id of the variant matches the fetched product
6. Fetch the option by id from ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options
7. Validate option belongs to the variant (product_variant_id matches)
8. Verify the option is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null)
9. Delete the option record from ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options
10. Return 204 No Content or the deleted option if requested

Business rules:
- Only the product owner (seller) can delete options
- Cannot delete options from variants with pending transactions (paid/shipped order items, pending cancellation/refund requests) - this prevents data inconsistency in order fulfillment
- The variant itself must remain intact after option deletion
- CASCADE delete configured on variant deletion automatically removes options
- Option deletion does not create a snapshot per requirements

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific historical snapshot of a product, showing the complete state of the product as it existed at a particular moment in time.

This operation provides read-only access to product snapshots for audit trails, dispute resolution, and historical reference. Each snapshot captures the product's name, description, pricing (base and sale prices), status, and tags at the time the snapshot was created. The response includes the exact snapshot timestamp for chronological ordering.

Access to product snapshots is restricted based on actor roles and permissions. Product owners (sellers) can only view snapshots of their own products to review their product's change history. Platform administrators have unrestricted access to view snapshots of any product on the platform for oversight and compliance purposes.

Snapshots are immutable records that remain accessible even after a product is deleted, ensuring historical data integrity for order disputes and audit requirements. The snapshot data can be used to reconstruct what a customer saw when purchasing a product, verify price changes over time, and track modification history.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Retrieve a specific product snapshot by ID.

1. Validate that productId matches the snapshot's referenced product.
2. Verify authentication - user must be logged in as seller or admin.
3. Authorization check:
   - If user is seller: verify ownership (user.id == product.seller_id)
   - If user is admin: allow access to any product snapshot
4. Query ecommerce_mall_product_snapshots by snapshotId.
5. Join with ecommerce_mall_products to verify product exists and get seller_id for ownership validation.
6. Return snapshot data with all fields: name, slug, description, base_price, sale_price, status, tags, and timestamps.
7. If snapshot not found: return 404 Not Found.
8. If user lacks permission: return 403 Forbidden.

Business rules:
- Snapshots are immutable - never modified or deleted once created.
- Snapshots remain accessible even if the product is deleted.
- Access is logged for audit purposes.

Error handling:
- Invalid UUID format in path parameters: 400 Bad Request.
- Snapshot not found: 404 Not Found.
- Unauthorized access: 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden.
- Database query failure: 500 Internal Server Error.

- 403 Forbidden: If the actor is not authorized to view this snapshot (not the product owner and not an admin)
- 404 Not Found: If the product or variant does not exist

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of inventory movement records for products sold by the authenticated seller.

This operation provides comprehensive inventory tracking capabilities including restock operations, sales deductions, returns, cancellations, and stock adjustments. Each record in the list represents a single stock movement event with details about the quantity change, reason for the movement, and remaining inventory level after the transaction.

The inventory records serve as an immutable audit trail for all stock movements - records cannot be modified after creation to ensure data integrity for dispute resolution and financial reconciliation. However, the system supports soft delete via the deleted_at field for data preservation purposes. Soft-deleted records are filtered out by default in seller views while remaining accessible to administrators for oversight and compliance requirements.

Records include references to related orders, cancellation requests, and refund requests when applicable, enabling complete traceability of inventory changes back to their source transactions.

   - variantId: Filter by specific product variant

   - type: Filter by transaction type (INCOMING, OUTGOING, ADJUSTMENT)
   - dateRange: Filter created_at within specified date range
   - quantityChangeRange: Filter by quantity change amount range

3. Apply sorting: Support sorting by created_at, quantity_change, reason
4. Apply pagination: cursor-based or offset-based pagination with configurable page size
5. Include summary fields: id, variant reference, quantity_change, remaining_quantity, reason, type, description, created_at
6. Order by created_at descending by default (newest first)

Security: Ensure seller authentication and verify ownership of all returned inventory records.

Error handling:
- Return 400 for invalid filter parameters
- Return 401 for unauthenticated requests
- Return 404 if seller has no inventory records matching filters

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific inventory record from a product variant's stock movement history.

This endpoint allows sellers to view the complete details of an individual inventory record that tracks a specific stock movement event. Each inventory record represents a single change to the stock quantity of a product variant, whether it's a restock (positive change), sale (negative change), return, cancellation, refund, or manual adjustment.

The returned inventory record includes the quantity change amount, the type of transaction (INCOMING, OUTGOING, or ADJUSTMENT), the reason category (RESTOCK, SALE, RETURN, CANCELLATION, ADJUSTMENT, DAMAGE, LOSS, etc.), and the remaining stock quantity after this movement. It also contains timestamps for when the record was created and last updated.

Inventory records may optionally reference related orders, cancellation requests, or refund requests that triggered the stock movement. These foreign key references are included in the response to provide context about what transaction caused this particular stock change.

All inventory records are immutable audit trail entries with respect to their core business data (quantity_change, reason, type, remaining_quantity) which cannot be modified once created. However, the system supports soft deletion via the deleted_at field for data preservation purposes while maintaining a complete historical record.

Inventory records are referenced by order items, cancellation requests, and refund requests to track stock movements throughout the order lifecycle.

Create a new inventory record to track stock movements for a product variant, typically used for restocking incoming inventory from suppliers or processing returned items.

This operation enables sellers to manually increase inventory by recording positive quantity changes in the immutable inventory audit trail. According to the database schema, each inventory record contains a quantity_change field indicating the stock movement direction (positive for incoming, negative for outgoing), a reason field categorizing the movement type, and a type field for transaction classification.

Sellers must specify the target product variant, the quantity being added, and a reason categorizing the stock movement (such as "supplier delivery" or "returned items processed"). The system preserves the remaining inventory quantity after the movement for historical reference.

All inventory records are stored in the ecommerce_mall_inventory_records table and cannot be manually deleted, ensuring data integrity for financial audits and dispute resolution. The table supports soft delete through the deleted_at field, but inventory records are preserved indefinitely as required by business rules for complete stock movement history.

operations.specification:
Create a new inventory record in the ecommerce_mall_inventory_records table with the following steps:

1. Validate that the requesting seller is authorized to manage the target product variant (seller owns the product)
2. Verify the product variant exists by querying ecommerce_mall_product_variants table
3. Validate quantity_change is a positive integer (restocking operation)
4. Validate reason is provided and matches allowed categories (RESTOCK, RETURN, etc.)
5. Calculate remaining_quantity by adding quantity_change to the current variant's stock level
6. Insert new record with type='INCOMING' and reason provided
7. Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp (UTC)
8. Return the complete created inventory record including id, all field values, and timestamps

Business rules:
- quantity_change must be > 0 for restocking operations
- reason field is required and must be non-empty
- variant must belong to a product owned by the requesting seller
- All fields except id and timestamps are required in request body

Error scenarios:
- 403: Seller does not own the product variant
- 404: Product variant not found
- 400: Invalid quantity_change (not positive) or missing required fields

responseBody.description: Created inventory record with all fields including system-generated values (id, created_at, updated_at)

requestBody.description: Inventory record creation data including product variant reference, quantity change, reason, and optional description

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of immutable snapshot records for a specific inventory record. Snapshot records provide an audit trail of inventory changes, capturing point-in-time state including quantity, reserved quantity, reason codes, and timestamps.

This operation supports advanced search capabilities including date range filtering, reason code filtering, and sorting options. The response includes summarized snapshot information optimized for list displays in audit trail views and dispute resolution workflows.

Snapshots are automatically created when inventory records are modified and cannot be manually created, modified, or deleted by any user. This operation allows customers, sellers, and administrators to view historical inventory changes for reconciliation and investigation purposes.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_inventory_snapshots table filtered by inventory_record_id parameter.

Apply search filters:
- Date range filtering on created_at timestamp
- Reason code filtering using partial string matching
- Quantity range filtering (minimum/maximum quantity)
- Variant ID filtering (denormalized variant_id field)

Sorting:
- Sort by created_at ascending (oldest first) or descending (newest first)
- Sort by quantity in ascending or descending order

Pagination:
- Cursor-based pagination for efficient large result set handling
- Configurable page size (default: 20, maximum: 100)
- Include total count and pagination metadata

Validation:
- Verify inventory_record_id exists in ecommerce_mall_inventory_records
- Return 404 if inventory record not found
- Return 403 if user lacks authorization for inventory record

Security:
- Sellers can view snapshots for inventory records of their own product variants
- Customers can view snapshots for inventory records in their orders
- Administrators and superAdmins can view all snapshots
- Verify actor authorization before returning results

Performance:
- Use index on inventory_record_id for fast filtering
- Use index on created_at for efficient date range queries
- Limit result set to configured page size
- Return summary fields only (not full snapshot details)

responseBody.description: Paginated list of snapshot summaries with historical inventory state information

operations.description:
Retrieve a single inventory snapshot record that captures the state of an inventory movement at a specific point in time.

This operation returns the complete historical state of an inventory snapshot including the quantity remaining at the time of snapshot creation, reserved quantity, reason code, notes, and timestamp. Snapshots serve as an immutable audit trail for inventory movements and are essential for dispute resolution, stock reconciliation, and compliance auditing.

**Authorization**: Sellers can only view snapshots of inventory records associated with product variants owned by their products. Platform administrators have full access to all inventory snapshots across the platform.

**Relationship**: Each snapshot is linked to a parent inventory record via the `inventory_record_id` field, which itself belongs to a product variant through the `variant` relationship. The snapshot includes denormalized `variant_id` for efficient historical queries without database joins.

**Immutability**: Unlike regular inventory records, snapshots are append-only and never deleted or modified once created. This ensures the integrity of the audit trail and provides reliable evidence for dispute resolution.
operations.name: at

Query the ecommerce_mall_inventory_snapshots table to retrieve the specific snapshot identified by snapshotId.

Validate that both inventoryRecordId and snapshotId parameters exist and are valid UUIDs.

Verify ownership or access permissions - only the seller who owns the associated product variant or platform administrators should be able to view inventory snapshots.

Perform a database query filtering by both inventory_record_id (matching the provided inventoryRecordId) and id (matching the provided snapshotId).

Return the snapshot with all fields including denormalized variant_id, quantity, reserved_quantity, reason, notes, and created_at timestamp.

Return 404 Not Found if no snapshot exists with the matching combination of inventoryRecordId and snapshotId.

Return 403 Forbidden if the requesting actor does not have permission to view this snapshot (sellers can only view snapshots for their own variants, administrators have full access).

responseBody.description: Inventory snapshot with complete historical state at time of creation

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of customer purchase orders.

This operation provides comprehensive search capabilities for order management including status filtering, date range queries, customer identification, payment status checks, and shipment tracking. Users can search by order number, customer email, or product identifiers to locate specific transactions.

Supports advanced filtering on order totals, shipping methods, and fulfillment status. The paginated response includes order summary information optimized for dashboard displays and order management interfaces.

Customers can view their own orders, while sellers can view orders for products they manage, and administrators have full platform-wide access to all orders.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_orders table with pagination and filtering.

Apply search filters on status (pending, paid, shipped, cancelled, refunded), date ranges (created_at, updated_at, paid_at, shipped_at, cancelled_at), customer ID or email, payment method, shipping method, order totals within range, and active/cancelled status.

Join with ecommerce_mall_order_items for order item statistics (item count, total quantity) if requested.

Optionally join with ecommerce_mall_customers for customer summary information (display name, email) when authorization permits.

Order by created_at descending by default, with support for custom sort fields (status, total_amount, customer_name).

Implement cursor-based pagination for large result sets with configurable page size (default 20, max 100).

Validate authorization: customers see only their own orders, sellers see orders containing their products, admins and super admins see all orders.

Return 200 with paginated order summaries on success.

Return 401 if unauthorized.

Return 400 if pagination parameters are invalid.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order summaries

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific order from the ecommerce platform.

This operation returns complete order information including the order number, overall status, customer details, line items with pricing, shipping information, and fulfillment tracking data. The order number is a unique identifier assigned at order creation and is used for customer reference and support inquiries.

Only the customer who created the order can view its complete details, unless the requester is an administrator who has platform-wide order visibility. Order information includes the relationship to the customer, all order items with product references, and any associated shipment tracking information.

If the order does not exist or the requesting user does not have permission to access it, the operation will return an appropriate error response. The order status reflects the current state of the entire order as derived from the statuses of all order items within it.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_orders table for the order with the specified UUID. Join with ecommerce_mall_order_items to retrieve line items, and join with ecommerce_mall_shipments for shipping information if available.

Apply authorization check: if the requester is a customer, verify ownership (customer_id matches the authenticated customer). If the requester is an admin, allow access to any order. If the requester is a seller, only provide order items that belong to their products.

Return the complete order object including all order items with product snapshot references, shipping details, and calculated totals. Ensure the order status is current based on the latest item statuses.

Handle not-found cases by returning 404 if the order UUID does not exist. Handle authorization failures by returning 403 if the customer is not the order owner.

responseBody.description: Complete order information with items and shipping details

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of order items within a specific order.

This operation provides detailed item-level information for all order items belonging to the specified order, including product details, variant information, pricing, quantities, and current status.

Supports filtering by status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded), product variant, and sorting options. Response includes comprehensive item data needed for order history views, seller fulfillment interfaces, and administrative oversight.

Each order item represents a distinct product variant purchase within the order and can have its own independent status and cancellation/refund requests.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_order_items table filtering by ecommerce_mall_order_id (path parameter).

Apply optional filters from requestBody:
- status: filter by item status (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded)
- product_name: partial match on product name
- variant_sku: exact match on variant SKU
- date_range: filter by created_at timestamp range

Sort results by created_at (descending) by default, support custom sorting.

Apply pagination with configurable page size (default 20, max 100).

Join with snapshot tables for immutable product/variant data as denormalized in order_items.

Authorization: authenticated customers can view their own orders' items, sellers can view items for their products, administrators can view all items.

Handle 404 if order does not exist or user lacks access.

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific order item within an order.

This operation returns complete details for a single order item identified by its order ID and item ID. The response includes denormalized product information (product name, SKU, variant name), quantity purchased, unit price at purchase time, total price for the line item, and timestamps. Each order item contains references to snapshots of the product, variant, and seller as they existed at order creation time, ensuring historical accuracy.

Authorization requirements vary by actor type: customers can view order items only from orders they created, sellers can view order items only for products they own, and administrators with elevated privileges can view all order items regardless of ownership. This ensures data isolation and privacy between customers and sellers.

The operation supports order item identification using the unique order number format or UUID-based order ID. When the order item does not exist, is not accessible to the actor, or has been soft deleted, the operation returns a 404 Not Found error. Use this endpoint to display order item details in customer order history, seller sales reports, or administrative review interfaces.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_order_items table to retrieve the order item matching the given orderId and itemId path parameters.

Authorization Logic:
1. Retrieve the order to determine ownership
2. Check actor type and permissions:
   - For customer actors: verify order.customer_id matches authenticated customer ID
   - For seller actors: verify the order item's seller_snapshot_id matches authenticated seller ID or product belongs to seller
   - For admin/superAdmin actors: bypass ownership checks, allow viewing all items
3. Return 404 if authorization fails or order item does not exist

Query Implementation:
1. Fetch order from ecommerce_mall_orders by orderId
2. Fetch order item from ecommerce_mall_order_items by itemId and verify it belongs to the order
3. Include denormalized fields: product_name, product_sku, variant_name, quantity, unit_price, total_price
4. Verify deleted_at is NULL to ensure item is not soft deleted

Error Handling:
- Return 404 if order does not exist
- Return 404 if order item does not exist or does not belong to the order
- Return 404 if item is soft deleted (deleted_at is not NULL)
- Return 403 if authenticated actor lacks authorization to view the order item

Return the order item record with all fields including timestamps and snapshot references.

responseBody.description: Complete order item details including product information, variant details, pricing, and quantities

This operation provides comprehensive oversight into the evolution of an order's state throughout its lifecycle. Each snapshot captures the order's data at specific points in time including when it was created, when status changed, and when payment status was updated.

Administrators can use this endpoint to investigate orders, resolve disputes, or verify transaction history. The response includes all snapshots ordered by creation timestamp, enabling reconstruction of the complete order timeline.

Supports filtering by status to retrieve snapshots where the order had a particular status, and supports pagination for efficient browsing of historical records.

Sort by created_at DESC by default to show newest snapshots first. Apply status filter if provided to only return snapshots matching the specified status value. This operation returns immutable historical data about an order including customer information, shipping address, payment details, and order totals as they existed when the snapshot was created. Snapshots are preserved indefinitely for audit trails, dispute resolution, and historical reporting.

Customers can view snapshots from their own orders in their order history to see historical states. Administrators can view snapshots from any order on the platform for oversight, audit, and dispute resolution purposes.

The snapshot includes denormalized fields such as customer name, email, and shipping address that remain unchanged even if the underlying customer or address records are later modified. This ensures historical accuracy for dispute resolution and compliance.

Snapshots cannot be modified or deleted once created. They are append-only records that form part of the platform's immutable audit trail.

Retrieve a chronological list of snapshots for a specific order item within your order, showing the historical changes to the order item's product details, pricing, and status.

This operation provides access to the complete change history of an order item that you purchased, including snapshots of the product name, description, variant options, prices, and seller profile as they existed at different points in time. Each snapshot captures the exact state of the order item when a change occurred, with timestamps for dispute resolution and audit purposes.

You can view snapshots for order items in your own orders to verify purchase details and maintain personal records. This includes historical product information, prices, and variant details at the time of each change. If the original product has been deleted from the platform by the seller, the snapshots remain accessible to you and preserve the product information for your order history.

Snapshots are preserved indefinitely even after the original product is deleted from the platform, ensuring that your order history remains accurate for legal compliance and dispute resolution purposes. The immutable snapshot records cannot be modified or deleted, providing a reliable audit trail of your purchase history.

Access to order item snapshots is controlled by order ownership and administrative privileges. Customers can only view snapshots of order items from orders they placed. Sellers can view snapshots of their own products as referenced in orders. Administrators and super administrators have full access to all order item snapshots across the platform for oversight and dispute resolution.

Each order item snapshot preserves denormalized data from the product snapshot, variant snapshot, and seller snapshot that were active at the time of purchase. This ensures historical accuracy even if the original products are later modified or deleted.

- Admin: Can view all order item snapshots for oversight purposes
