operations.description:
Create a new shipment for order items from a single seller.

This operation allows sellers to create shipments for their order items that are in paid status. Each shipment represents a physical package being delivered to a customer and must contain only order items from the same seller. Different sellers always ship separately, even when their products are in the same customer order.

When creating a shipment, the seller must provide carrier tracking information including the carrier name, and optionally the carrier phone number and website URL for tracking. All order items included in the shipment will share identical tracking information and will be marked as shipped once the shipment is created.

The operation validates that all selected order items belong to the authenticated seller and have paid status (not cancelled, not shipped, and not refunded). Attempting to create shipments for order items from different sellers or with invalid statuses will result in a validation error.

Upon successful creation, the system records the shipment with status 'pending', creates junction records linking the shipment to each order item in the ecommerce_mall_shipments_order_items table, and updates the status of all included order items to shipped. These order items can no longer be cancelled by the customer after being shipped.

Related operations:
- GET /ecommerce_mall/seller/shipments - View shipments created by the seller
- GET /ecommerce_mall/seller/orders - View orders with items requiring shipping
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new shipment record for order items from a single seller.

Service layer logic:
1. Validate seller authorization - check that the authenticated seller is authorized to create shipments
2. For each order item ID in the request:
   - Verify order item exists and is not soft-deleted
   - Verify order item's seller_snapshot_id matches the authenticated seller's ID
   - Verify order item status is 'paid' (not cancelled, not shipped, not refunded)
   - Ensure all order items in the request belong to the same seller
3. Validate tracking information - at least carrier_name must be provided
4. Create shipment record with status='pending', carrier information, and order item mappings
5. Create shipment items records in ecommerce_mall_shipments_order_items junction table for each order item
6. Update all included order items to status='shipped'
7. Return the created shipment with all relationships loaded

Database operations:
- INSERT into ecommerce_mall_shipments
- INSERT into ecommerce_mall_shipments_order_items (one record per order item)
- UPDATE ecommerce_mall_order_items set status='shipped' where id in request

Business rules and validation:
- Reject if any order item is from a different seller
- Reject if any order item is cancelled, already shipped, or refunded
- Reject if tracking information is incomplete (carrier_name required)
- Prevent duplicate shipment creation for same order items

Error handling:
- 400 Bad Request: Validation failures (wrong seller, invalid status, missing tracking)
- 404 Not Found: Order item or seller not found
- 409 Conflict: Order item already included in another shipment

responseBody.description: Created shipment record with full details including carrier information, linked order items, and shipment status

requestBody.description: Shipment creation request with tracking information and order items to include

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of shipments for the authenticated seller with search, filter, and sort capabilities.

This operation provides comprehensive shipment visibility for sellers to manage their fulfillment workflow. Sellers can view all shipments they have created, track their delivery status, monitor carrier information, and filter by various criteria such as status, date ranges, and carrier.

The response includes essential shipment information optimized for list display, including status, carrier details, tracking count, and key timestamps. Each shipment can be accessed in detail via its individual detail endpoint.

Sellers can only view their own shipments. The system enforces data isolation to prevent sellers from accessing another seller's fulfillment data. Shipments are automatically included in the results based on the seller_id relationship defined in the database schema.

Related Operations:
- GET /shipments/{shipmentId} - View detailed information for a specific shipment
- GET /shipments/{shipmentId}/trackingCodes - View all tracking codes for a shipment
- GET /orders/{orderId}/shipments - View all shipments for a specific order
- PATCH /shipments - Create new shipment for order items (separate create endpoint)

Search and Filter Capabilities:
Support filtering by shipment status (pending, in-transit, delivered, failed, cancelled), carrier name, date ranges for creation, shipping, and delivery timestamps. Optional sorting by any timestamp field or status.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_shipments table filtering by seller_id (from authenticated seller context) and optional search criteria.

Business Logic:
1. Filter shipments where ecommerce_mall_seller_id matches the authenticated seller's ID
2. Apply optional filters: status, carrier_name, date ranges (shipped_at, delivered_at, created_at), order_id reference
3. Join with ecommerce_mall_order_items via shipment_id to include item counts
4. Join with tracking_codes table to summarize tracking count per shipment
5. Support pagination with cursor-based or offset-based approach
6. Support sorting by created_at (default), shipped_at, delivered_at, status
7. Return summary fields optimized for list display

Validation:
- Reject if seller attempts to access another seller's shipments
- Return empty list if no shipments match criteria
- Ensure all timestamps are returned in UTC ISO 8601 format

Edge Cases:
- Handle shipments with null carrier information
- Handle shipments with no tracking codes yet
- Handle deleted_at timestamps for soft-deleted shipments (exclude from results)

responseBody.description: Paginated list of shipment summaries with essential fulfillment information

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering shipments

Retrieve detailed information about a specific shipment in the marketplace.

This operation returns the complete shipment record including carrier tracking information (carrier name, phone, website), current delivery status (pending, in-transit, delivered, failed, or cancelled), and temporal tracking fields (shipped_at, delivered_at, estimated_delivery_at). The response includes the delivery address and references to the parent order and fulfilling seller.

Shipment information is primarily accessed by sellers who created the shipment (for fulfillment management), customers who are the recipients (for delivery tracking), and platform administrators (for logistics monitoring). The endpoint validates that the shipment exists and returns not found errors for invalid shipment IDs.

This operation should be used after identifying a shipment through list operations (GET /shipments), or when direct shipment ID is available from order confirmation, customer account view, or seller dashboard.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_shipments table by id UUID parameter.

Validation and Business Logic:
1. Verify shipmentId is a valid UUID format
2. Query shipment record by id (including deleted_at != null check for soft delete if actor permissions allow)
3. If shipment not found, return 404 Not Found
4. For soft-deleted shipments (deleted_at is not null), apply actor-specific access rules:
   - Admin/superAdmin: can view deleted shipments for audit purposes
   - Seller/customer: may have restricted access to deleted shipments
5. Join with ecommerce_mall_orders to include order reference metadata if needed
6. Join with ecommerce_mall_sellers to include seller reference metadata if needed
7. Return shipment record with all fields (id, ecommerce_mall_order_id, ecommerce_mall_seller_id, carrier_name, carrier_phone, carrier_website, status, shipped_at, delivered_at, estimated_delivery_at, delivery_address, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at)

Edge Cases:
- Shipment with null carrier fields: return entity with nullable values
- Shipment status: return as-is from database (pending, in-transit, delivered, failed, cancelled)
- Null temporal fields (shipped_at, delivered_at): return null values in response
- Soft-deleted shipment: apply actor-specific access control policy

operations.description:
Update an existing shipment record with modified delivery information.

This operation allows authorized sellers to update shipment details such as delivery address and estimated delivery date. Tracking information (carrier name, phone, website) cannot be modified after shipment creation per business rules.

Authorized actors: seller (own shipments only), admin (all shipments)

The operation validates that the requesting seller owns the shipment, that requested status transitions are valid, and that only updatable fields are modified. Tracking details (carrier_name, carrier_phone, carrier_website) are immutable after creation and will be rejected if included in the update payload.

Related operations:
- GET /shipments/{shipmentId} - Retrieve current shipment details before updating
- PATCH /shipments - List shipments with filters for monitoring
- GET /shipments/{shipmentId}/trackingCodes - View tracking codes for the shipment
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Validate authentication: requester must be seller or admin actor
2. Load shipment by ID from ecommerce_mall_shipments
3. Verify authorization: seller must own shipment (ecommerce_mall_seller_id == authenticated seller ID), admin can update any shipment
4. Validate status transition: if status is being updated, check it's a valid transition from current status
   - Valid transitions: pending->in-transit, in-transit->delivered, in-transit->failed, pending->cancelled, in-transit->cancelled
5. Filter update payload: reject any attempt to modify carrier_name, carrier_phone, carrier_website (tracking info is immutable)
6. Update allowed fields only: delivery_address, estimated_delivery_at
7. Set updated_at timestamp to current UTC time
8. Create snapshot record in ecommerce_mall_shipment_snapshots before applying changes (audit trail)
9. Apply UPDATE to ecommerce_mall_shipments table
10. Return complete updated shipment object

Error handling:
- 404 Not Found: shipment_id does not exist or has been soft deleted
- 403 Forbidden: seller attempting to update another seller's shipment
- 400 Bad Request: attempting to modify immutable tracking fields, invalid status transition, or invalid data formats
11. Transaction: all changes must be atomic (shipment update + snapshot creation)

responseBody.description: Complete updated shipment object with all fields

parameters.name: shipmentId

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered list of order items contained within a specific shipment.

This operation returns all order items that are included in the shipment identified by the shipmentId path parameter. Each order item record contains the shipped quantity, which may differ from the original order quantity if partial shipment occurred.

Sellers can use this endpoint to view the breakdown of order items in their shipments for fulfillment tracking and customer service. The response supports pagination, filtering by shipped quantity status, and sorting options for managing large shipments.

Shipment items are managed through the parent shipment entity. This operation only retrieves existing items - creation and deletion occur through shipment creation and fulfillment workflows, not through direct item operations.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_shipments_order_items table filtering by shipment_id equal to the shipmentId path parameter.

Apply pagination with configurable page size (default: 20) and page number for cursor-based or offset-based pagination.

Apply optional filters on shipped_quantity if provided in the request body.

Apply optional sorting on shipped_quantity or created_at if specified in the request body.

Return order items with their shipped_quantity, timestamps, and references to parent shipment and order item.

Validate that the shipmentId exists and that the requesting seller has access to this shipment.

Enforce that only the seller who created the shipment (or an admin) can query shipment items.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of order items contained in the shipment with shipped quantities.

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific order item within a shipment.

This operation returns comprehensive information about an order item that is included in a particular shipment, including the order item's product details, quantity, price, and its current shipping status. The response includes the shipment's tracking information and the associated order context.

The endpoint verifies that the order item exists and is actually included in the specified shipment through the shipments_order_items junction table. Only users who own the order or are the seller responsible for the shipment can access this information.

Customers can use this endpoint to track individual items within their shipments. Sellers can use it to view fulfillment details for their shipped items. The operation returns both the order item data and the shipment context in a single response.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the shipments_order_items junction table to verify the relationship between the specified shipment and order item.

Perform a JOIN query that includes:
- shipments table data (trackingCarrier, trackingNumber, status, createdAt)
- order_items table data (quantity, unitPrice, productSnapshot, variantSnapshot)
- orders table data (orderNumber, orderDate, totalAmount, status)
- products table data (name, price, seller reference)

Validate that:
1. The shipment exists in ecommerce_mall_shipments table
2. The order item exists in ecommerce_mall_order_items table
3. The shipments_order_items junction record exists linking both entities
4. The requesting user has authorization (owns the order or is the shipment's seller)

Return 404 if the relationship doesn't exist or the entity doesn't exist.
Return 403 if the user lacks authorization.

Construct response DTO IShipmentOrderItem combining shipment tracking info with order item details.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of shipment audit trail snapshots for a specific delivery shipment.

This operation provides access to historical state changes for a shipment, including carrier information updates, tracking number changes, status transitions, and delivery milestones. Each snapshot captures the complete state of the shipment at a specific point in time, enabling dispute resolution, delivery verification, and audit compliance.

The operation supports advanced filtering by shipment status (pending, in transit, delivered, exception, returned), date ranges on snapshot creation or delivery dates, and carrier name. Sellers who own the shipment and platform administrators can access these snapshots for tracking purposes, dispute investigations, or delivery verification.

Each snapshot includes a created_at timestamp that allows reconstruction of the shipment's complete history when sorted chronologically. The response is paginated to support efficient browsing of large audit trails, with support for custom page sizes and sorting options to prioritize recent changes or specific status transitions.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_shipment_snapshots table filtered by shipmentId (ecommerce_mall_shipment_id field).

Filtering:
- Apply optional status filter (pending, in_transit, delivered, exception, returned)
- Apply optional date range on created_at timestamp
- Apply optional tracking_number search (partial match)
- Apply optional carrier_name filter

Sorting:
- Default sort by created_at descending (most recent first)
- Allow ascending/descending order
- Allow sort by status, shipped_date, actual_delivery_date

Pagination:
- Cursor-based or offset-based pagination
- Configurable page size (default 20, max 100)
- Return total count, page number, page size

Authorization:
- Verify caller is an admin, or
- Verify caller is a customer who owns the order associated with this shipment

Response includes:
- Paginated list of snapshot summaries with essential fields
- Full shipment state reconstruction capability via version field
- Timestamp for audit trail verification

responseBody.description: Paginated list of shipment snapshot summaries

parameters.description: UUID identifier of the shipment whose snapshots are being retrieved
parameters.name: shipmentId

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific historical snapshot of a shipment for dispute resolution and audit trail purposes.

This operation returns a point-in-time record of a shipment's complete state at the moment a snapshot was created. Snapshots capture immutable historical data including carrier information, tracking numbers, shipment status, package dimensions, delivery details, and timestamps. Each snapshot represents a frozen moment in the shipment's lifecycle.

The snapshot is used for dispute resolution to verify what the shipment state was at specific times, such as when a customer claims the package was delivered on a different date than recorded, or when there's a dispute about package condition upon delivery. Administrators use snapshots for fraud investigations, compliance audits, and regulatory reporting.

Access to snapshots is controlled by actor permissions. Customers can only view snapshots for shipments associated with their orders. Sellers can view snapshots for shipments they created. Administrators and super administrators have access to view snapshots for any shipment on the platform, including those from other sellers or customers involved in disputes.

Snapshots are read-only historical records and cannot be modified. They provide an authoritative source of truth for shipment state at specific points in time.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_shipment_snapshots table by snapshotId.

Authorization:
1. Validate actor is authenticated (customer, seller, admin, or superAdmin)
2. For customer actors: Verify the snapshot's parent shipment is associated with an order owned by the customer
3. For seller actors: Verify the snapshot's parent shipment was created by the seller
4. For admin/superAdmin actors: Grant access to any snapshot without restrictions

Query execution:
1. Fetch the snapshot record from ecommerce_mall_shipment_snapshots using snapshotId
2. Join with ecommerce_mall_shipments to verify parent shipment existence and ownership
3. For customer/seller authorization, join with ecommerce_mall_orders to establish the relationship chain
4. Return the complete snapshot record with all fields: id, tracking_number, carrier_name, carrier_contact, status, estimated_delivery_date, actual_delivery_date, shipped_date, tracking_url, shipping_method, weight_kg, dimensions, delivery_address, signature fields, delivery_notes, exception_description, and created_at

Error handling:
- Return 404 if snapshotId does not exist
- Return 404 if parent shipment was deleted (orphaned snapshot)
- Return 403 if actor lacks authorization to view this snapshot
- Return 401 if actor is not authenticated

responseBody.description: Complete historical snapshot record containing the full state of a shipment at a specific point in time

parameters.description: The UUID of the parent shipment this snapshot belongs to
parameters.name: shipmentId

operations.description:
Update the carrier tracking information for a specific shipment.

This operation allows sellers to modify the tracking codes associated with their shipments when shipping order items to customers. Each shipment can have multiple carrier tracking codes stored in the tracking codes table, supporting scenarios where the primary carrier is supplemented with sub-carrier tracking information.

Sellers must verify ownership of the shipment before updating tracking information. The operation replaces all existing tracking codes for the shipment with the new set provided in the request body. This ensures the tracking information remains consistent and up-to-date throughout the delivery lifecycle.

The tracking codes include the carrier name and tracking code for each carrier. This information enables customers and administrators to track the shipment's delivery progress through the carrier's tracking system.
operations.name: updateTrackingCodes
operations.specification:
Update tracking codes for the specified shipment by performing the following steps:

1. Retrieve the shipment record from ecommerce_mall_shipments by ID
2. Verify the requesting seller owns this shipment (ecommerce_mall_seller_id matches the seller's account)
3. Verify the shipment exists and has not been deleted (deleted_at is null)
4. Delete all existing tracking code records from ecommerce_mall_shipment_tracking_codes for this shipment_id
5. Insert new tracking code records from the request body, ensuring no duplicate tracking_code values exist for this shipment
6. Update the shipment's updated_at timestamp
7. Return the complete shipment object including all newly created tracking codes

Business Rules:
- Only the owning seller can update tracking codes for their shipments
- Trackers cannot be updated after the shipment status is 'delivered'
- Each tracking code must be unique within the shipment
- The request body must contain at least one valid tracking code
- Carrier name and tracking code are required fields for each tracking code entry

Error Handling:
- Return 404 if shipment does not exist
- Return 403 if the seller does not own the shipment
- Return 400 if any tracking code is missing required fields or contains duplicates
- Return 409 if a tracking code conflicts with an existing code (should not happen due to unique constraint)

This operation returns the tracking code record associated with a shipment, including the carrier name and tracking number. Customers can view tracking information for shipments containing their order items, sellers can view tracking codes for shipments they created, and administrators can access all tracking codes across the platform.

The tracking code is uniquely identified within a shipment by its combination of shipment ID and tracking code ID. Each tracking code record contains the carrier name (e.g., FedEx, UPS, DHL, USPS) and the unique tracking code provided by that carrier for shipment delivery status updates.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_shipment_tracking_codes table for the specific tracking code record identified by trackingCodeId.

Validation logic:
1. Verify the tracking code record exists
2. Verify the tracking code belongs to the specified shipment (matching shipment_id)
3. Check authorization based on actor type:
   - Sellers: Only allow access if they own the shipment
   - Customers: Only allow access if the shipment contains their order items
   - Administrators: Allow access to all tracking codes

Return the tracking code entity with carrier_name and tracking_code fields. If the tracking code does not exist or does not belong to the specified shipment, return a 404 error. If the actor does not have permission to view this tracking code, return a 403 error.

The tracking code record is a subsidiary entity managed through the parent shipment entity and is not independently created or modified by users. Tracking codes are permanently retained for audit and dispute resolution purposes.

operations.description:
Update tracking status information for shipment tracking updates.

This operation allows bulk updates to tracking update records associated with a specific shipment. Tracking updates represent carrier-provided status changes that record the delivery lifecycle from pending through delivered or failed states.

When carrier APIs push tracking status updates via webhooks, this operation processes and persists the new status information. It also supports manual updates by administrators who may need to correct or modify tracking information.

The operation supports selective updates through filtering criteria in the request body, allowing updates to be applied only to tracking updates matching specific conditions such as date ranges or current status values.

All tracking updates are permanently retained for audit and dispute resolution purposes. Soft delete is supported via the deleted_at field for tracking updates that are no longer relevant.

Related operations:
- GET /shipments/{shipmentId} must be pre-executed to retrieve the shipment context before updating tracking updates.
- GET /shipments/{shipmentId}/tracking-updates should be used to retrieve the current list of tracking updates before making updates.
operations.name: updateTrackingUpdates
operations.specification:
Query tracking updates belonging to the specified shipment by shipment_id (UUID). Apply updates to tracking_status and carrier_response fields based on request body criteria.

Validation rules:
1. Verify shipment exists and is not soft deleted before updating tracking updates
2. Validate tracking_status enum values: pending, in_transit, out_for_delivery, delivered, failed, exception
3. Ensure carrier_response is valid JSON string when provided (up to 80000 characters)
4. Check soft delete state - allow updates to active records only

Business logic:
1. Update tracking_status to new carrier-provided status
2. Persist carrier_response JSON payload from carrier API webhook
3. Update updated_at timestamp to current time
4. If tracking_status changed to delivered, automatically update shipment's delivered_at to current timestamp
5. If tracking_status changed to failed or cancelled, update shipment status accordingly

Query optimization:
1. Use compound index on (shipment_id, created_at) for efficient filtering
2. Filter by optional created_at range if provided in request
3. Filter by optional tracking_status if provided in request

Transaction handling:
1. Begin transaction before updating tracking updates
2. Apply all tracking update updates atomically
3. Update parent shipment's delivery timestamps if status changed to delivered/failed
4. Commit transaction after all updates complete successfully
5. Rollback on any validation or constraint violation

responseBody.description: Paginated list of updated tracking update summaries

parameters.name: shipmentId

requestBody.description: Update criteria and new values for tracking updates

Retrieve detailed tracking update information for a specific shipment delivery event.

This operation returns a single tracking update record that represents a status change in a shipment's delivery journey, such as the transition from 'in_transit' to 'out_for_delivery' or to 'delivered'. Tracking updates are automatically created when shipping carriers push status events to the platform via carrier API integration.

The tracking update contains the current tracking status, timestamp of the update, and the full carrier response payload in JSON format. This data is used by customers to monitor their delivery progress, by sellers to track shipment performance, and by administrators to monitor logistics operations across the platform.

Access to tracking updates is scoped to the shipment's context: customers can view tracking updates for shipments containing their order items, sellers can view updates for shipments they created, and administrators can view all shipments across the platform.

- If requester is customer: verify order_id of shipment exists in order_items where customer_id = requester.customer_id
- If requester is seller: verify ecommerce_mall_seller_id = requester.seller_id
- If requester is admin: allow access

Return 404 if record not found or access denied.

Do not include navigation properties (shipment relation) in response.

Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of customer reviews for a specific product.

This operation returns all active (non-deleted) reviews for the specified product, sorted by newest first. Each review includes the customer's rating (1-5 stars), optional title, review text, verification status, and author information.

Supports advanced filtering by rating range and verified purchase status. Results are paginated using cursor-based pagination for efficient handling of large review sets. The operation excludes soft-deleted reviews to maintain data integrity.

Customers can view reviews for any product on the platform. Reviews are displayed on product detail pages to help shoppers make informed purchasing decisions based on customer feedback.

Query ecommerce_mall_reviews table filtered by productId and deleted_at IS NULL.

Exclude soft-deleted reviews (deleted_at IS NULL).

Calculate average rating from non-deleted reviews for product display.
Return paginated results with total count for frontend pagination UI.

operations.description:
Retrieves a single product review by its unique identifier, displaying complete review information including rating, title, and content.

This operation provides detailed information about a specific customer review, enabling consumers to read product feedback and assess the helpfulness of written reviews. The returned review includes the star rating (1-5), optional title, full text content, verified purchase status, and timestamps for creation and last modification.

The operation respects data visibility rules based on the requester's authentication status and permissions. For unauthenticated or regular customers, only non-deleted reviews are returned, ensuring deleted content remains hidden from public view. Administrators and authorized personnel can access deleted reviews for moderation and dispute resolution purposes.

Deleted reviews that have been marked with a deletion timestamp are excluded from standard retrieval to maintain data privacy while preserving the audit trail for authorized actors with elevated privileges.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_reviews table for single review by UUID.

1. Validate reviewId is valid UUID format
2. Fetch review record from ecommerce_mall_reviews where id matches reviewId
3. For unauthenticated requests: Filter out reviews where deleted_at IS NOT NULL
4. For authenticated customer: Return review if customer_id matches authenticated user OR deleted_at IS NULL
5. For administrator: Return review regardless of deleted_at status
6. Load related customer profile (customer display name) via customer_id
7. If customer profile is deleted, set display name to 'deleted user'
8. Return review with all fields: id, customer_id, product_id, order_id, rating, title, body, is_verified_purchase, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at
9. Handle 404 if review not found or inaccessible due to deletion status
10. Handle 403 if customer attempts to access another customer's deleted review

Database query: SELECT * FROM ecommerce_mall_reviews WHERE id = :reviewId AND (deleted_at IS NULL OR :hasAdminAccess = true)

Join with customer table for display name resolution when rendering review author information.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of product reviews from the ecommerce platform.

This operation provides advanced search and filtering capabilities for product reviews, enabling customers to browse reviews for products they are interested in. Customers can filter reviews by product to see all reviews for a specific product, including their own and other customers' reviews.

The operation supports pagination with configurable page size and cursor-based navigation for efficient large result set handling. Results are sorted by newest first by default, but can be sorted by rating or creation date.

By default, only non-deleted reviews are returned. Reviews are soft-deleted (marked with deleted_at timestamp) rather than permanently removed, allowing for potential recovery and audit trail purposes. Deleted reviews are excluded from search results to maintain data privacy and business integrity.

Each returned review includes the rating (1-5 stars), title, body content, verification status, and timestamps. Related helpfulness vote counts can be calculated from the vote table for review quality assessment.

Customers must be authenticated to access this endpoint. By default, customers can only see reviews where the product_id matches products in their purchased orders, or they can view all product reviews by specifying a product_id filter. Customer identity filtering is restricted - customers can only view their own reviews by filtering with their customer_id.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_reviews table with the following logic:

1. Filter out deleted reviews where deleted_at IS NOT NULL
2. Apply customer_id filter if provided in request
3. Apply product_id filter if provided in request
4. Apply order_id filter if provided in request
5. Apply rating range filter (min_rating, max_rating) if provided
6. Apply text search on title and body fields using PostgreSQL full-text search or trigram similarity
7. Apply is_verified_purchase filter if provided
8. Apply review creation date range filter (from_created_at, to_created_at) if provided
9. Join with ecommerce_mall_review_helpfulness_votes to count helpfulness votes per review (optional)
10. Order results by created_at DESC by default, or by rating DESC if sort_by is 'rating'
11. Implement cursor-based pagination using created_at + id for deterministic ordering
12. Return only non-null deleted_at records (active reviews)
13. Apply row-level security: customers can only filter by their own reviews unless they have admin privileges

Service layer validations:
- Verify customer_id exists in ecommerce_mall_customers if provided
- Verify product_id exists in ecommerce_mall_products if provided
- Verify order_id exists in ecommerce_mall_orders if provided
- Validate rating range: min_rating >= 1, max_rating <= 5
- Validate pagination: page_size between 1 and 100
- Validate sorting: sort_by must be 'created_at' or 'rating'
- Validate direction: direction must be 'asc' or 'desc'

Query execution:
- Use PostgreSQL parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection
- Leverage composite index on (product_id, rating) for product rating queries
- Leverage index on (customer_id, created_at) for customer review browsing
- Use trigram GIN index on body field for text search
- Implement cursor-based pagination to avoid offset problems with large datasets
- Return review summaries with helpfulness vote counts aggregated from votes table

operations.description:
Create a new product review for a purchased item.

This operation allows authenticated customers to submit feedback about products they have purchased and received. A review consists of a star rating from 1 to 5, optional text content (title and body), and is associated with the customer, product, and order for verification purposes.

Customers must be authenticated to create reviews. The system verifies that the customer has purchased the product in an order with 'delivered' status before allowing review creation. Each customer can write only one review per product per order to prevent duplicate feedback.

The review rating is validated to ensure it falls within the 1-5 star range. The review body is required, while the title is optional. Upon successful creation, the review is immediately visible on the product detail page and contributes to the product's average rating calculation.

Every review edit or deletion creates a snapshot of the review state for audit trail and dispute resolution purposes.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new review record in ecommerce_mall_reviews table.

1. Validate customer authentication - reject if unauthenticated
2. Verify order item status is 'delivered' before allowing review creation
3. Validate uniqueness constraint - reject if customer already has a review for this product in this order
4. Validate rating is an integer between 1 and 5
5. Validate body text is provided and not empty
6. Set is_verified_purchase to true (order provides proof of purchase)
7. Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp
8. Insert record into ecommerce_mall_reviews table
9. Return the created review object with all fields including generated id
10. Transaction: wrap database insert in transaction to ensure data consistency

responseBody.description: The created review object with all fields including id and timestamps

requestBody.description: Review creation data including rating, title, and body content

operations.description:
Update an existing customer review by replacing its content.

This operation allows a customer to edit a review they have written. The update is applied to the review identified by the reviewId path parameter. Only the review owner can update their own review.

The operation creates an immutable snapshot of the review's previous state before applying changes, preserving the audit trail for dispute resolution purposes. Every edit operation records the old rating, title, and body content in the snapshot table.

The rating field must be an integer between 1 and 5 stars. If the rating or body is not provided in the request, those fields will not be updated. The title field is optional and may be omitted entirely.

After successful update, the review contributes to the product's average rating calculation. Deleted reviews are excluded from average calculations, so this operation only affects active reviews.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Validate authentication - customer must be logged in
2. Fetch review by id from ecommerce_mall_reviews where id = {reviewId}
3. Verify ownership - customer.id must equal review.customer_id
4. If review is soft-deleted (deleted_at is not null), return 400 error
5. Create snapshot in ecommerce_mall_review_snapshots:
   - snapshot_type = 'modified'
   - old_data = JSON.stringify previous review state (id, customer_id, product_id, order_id, rating, title, body, is_verified_purchase, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at)
   - new_data = to-be-updated state (will be updated after save)
   - changed_by_type = 'customer'
   - changed_by_id = authenticated customer.id
6. Validate rating if provided in request:
   - rating must be integer between 1 and 5 (inclusive)
   - return 400 if validation fails
7. Execute UPDATE on ecommerce_mall_reviews:
   - Set rating from request.rating if provided
   - Set title from request.title if provided
   - Set body from request.body if provided
   - Set updated_at to current UTC timestamp
   - Where id = {reviewId} AND deleted_at IS NULL
8. Query the updated review record with all fields
9. Return 200 with full review object

Error cases:
- 401 if customer not authenticated
- 404 if review not found or customer does not own it
- 400 if rating is out of range or review is soft-deleted
- 403 if trying to update another customer's review

responseBody.description: The updated review with all fields including the new values.

parameters.description: UUID of the review to update
parameters.name: reviewId

requestBody.description: Fields to update in the review. Only provided fields will be modified.

operations.description:
Delete a customer review from the product catalog.

This operation permanently removes a review from public view by marking it as deleted. The review is no longer displayed on the product detail page and is excluded from average rating calculations. The deleted review data is preserved in the system via soft deletion for audit trail and dispute resolution purposes.

Authorization: Customers can only delete their own reviews. Administrators can delete any review regardless of ownership.

When a review is deleted, a snapshot is created and preserved that records the original state of the review, including the rating, text content, and deletion timestamp. The snapshot remains accessible to the review owner and administrators for audit purposes.

After deletion, the review record persists in the database with the deleted_at timestamp populated, but is no longer visible in standard queries or API responses.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Verify authentication - customer must be authenticated or admin role
2. Locate review by reviewId (UUID)
3. Validate deletion authorization:
   - If authenticated customer: verify customer_id matches authenticated user ID
   - If authenticated admin: allow deletion of any review
   - Return 403 Forbidden if unauthorized
4. Check if review already deleted (deleted_at is not null)
   - If already deleted, return 404 Not Found (resource already removed)
5. Create snapshot record in ecommerce_mall_review_snapshots:
   - Capture current review state (id, customer_id, product_id, order_id, rating, title, body, is_verified_purchase, created_at, updated_at)
   - Set snapshot timestamp to current time
   - Set snapshot actor to deleted_by (customer_id or admin_id)
   - Mark snapshot type as 'deleted' for audit purposes
6. Soft delete the review:
   - Update deleted_at column to current timestamp
   - Do NOT modify other fields (preserve audit trail)
7. Invalidate any cached review data for the affected product
8. Recalculate product average rating excluding deleted reviews
9. Return 204 No Content to indicate successful deletion

Error handling:
- 404 Not Found: Review not found or already deleted
- 403 Forbidden: Customer attempting to delete another customer's review (non-admin)
- 401 Unauthorized: No valid authentication token

Transaction requirements:
- Snapshot creation and review soft deletion must occur in same transaction to ensure data consistency
- Rollback both operations if either fails

parameters.name: reviewId

prerequisites.description: Review must be created before it can be deleted. This POST operation creates the review that will subsequently be deleted by this DELETE operation.

operations.description:
Cast or update a helpfulness vote for a specific review. This operation allows authenticated customers to indicate whether they found a review helpful (true) or not helpful (false).

When a customer submits a helpfulness vote, the system checks whether they have previously voted on the same review. If no existing vote is found, a new helpfulness vote record is created. If the customer has already voted, the existing vote is updated with the new helpfulness value.

The unique constraint on customer_id and review_id ensures that each customer can vote at most once per review, preventing duplicate votes. This constraint is enforced at the database level to maintain data integrity.

The helpfulness votes are used to calculate aggregate helpfulness scores for reviews, which can be used for sorting reviews and assessing review quality. Reviews with higher helpfulness scores may be displayed more prominently in review lists.

Only authenticated customers can cast helpfulness votes. Unauthenticated visitors cannot access this endpoint.

If the target review does not exist, the operation returns a 404 Not Found error.

If the target review has been soft-deleted, the operation returns a 404 Not Found error.

If the customer is not authenticated, the operation returns a 401 Unauthorized error.
operations.name: updateHelpfulnessVote
operations.specification:
1. Authenticate the request to obtain the customer's ID from the session token
2. Validate that reviewId is a valid UUID format
3. Query ecommerce_mall_reviews table to verify the review exists and is not soft-deleted
4. Query ecommerce_mall_review_helpfulness_votes table for existing vote with customer_id = authenticated customer ID AND review_id = reviewId
5. If no existing vote found:
   a. INSERT new record into ecommerce_mall_review_helpfulness_votes with:
      - id: generated UUID
      - ecommerce_mall_customer_id: authenticated customer ID
      - ecommerce_mall_review_id: reviewId
      - helpfulness: boolean value from request body
      - created_at: current timestamp (NOW())
      - updated_at: current timestamp (NOW())
      - deleted_at: NULL
   b. Return the newly created helpfulness vote record
6. If existing vote found:
   a. UPDATE the existing record:
      - helpfulness: boolean value from request body
      - updated_at: current timestamp (NOW())
   b. Return the updated helpfulness vote record
7. Transactional boundary: Steps 5 or 6 must be executed in a single database transaction to ensure atomicity
8. Return the full helpfulness vote record including id, customer_id, review_id, helpfulness, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at

responseBody.description: The updated or created helpfulness vote record for the review

parameters.description: ID of the review being voted on
parameters.name: reviewId

requestBody.description: Whether the review was helpful (true) or not helpful (false)

operations.description:
Cast a helpfulness vote on a customer review to help assess review quality and improve sorting.

This operation allows authenticated customers to indicate whether they found a review helpful or not helpful. Each customer can submit exactly one vote per review, preventing duplicate votes from the same user on the same review.

The helpfulness votes contribute to the review's quality assessment and can be used to sort reviews by helpfulness on the product detail page. Reviews with more helpful votes are typically displayed more prominently.

The current authenticated customer is automatically associated with the vote - no customer identification is required in the request body.

If a customer has already voted on this review, the operation returns a conflict error. To change a vote, the existing vote must first be deleted and a new one created.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new helpfulness vote record in the ecommerce_mall_review_helpfulness_votes table.

Implementation steps:
1. Extract reviewId from path parameter and validate it exists in ecommerce_mall_reviews
2. Get the authenticated customer's ID from the session token (customer context)
3. Validate the customer hasn't already voted on this review by checking for existing record with (customer_id, review_id) composite key
4. Extract helpfulness boolean value from request body
5. Create new record with:
   - id: auto-generated UUID
   - ecommerce_mall_customer_id: from authenticated session
   - ecommerce_mall_review_id: from path parameter
   - helpfulness: from request body
   - created_at, updated_at: current timestamp
   - deleted_at: null (not soft deleted)
6. Return the created vote record with all fields populated

responseBody.description: The newly created helpfulness vote record with all fields populated

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of audit trail snapshots for a specific review.

This operation provides access to the immutable snapshot history that records all state changes to a review, including initial creation, edits, and helpfulness vote updates. Each snapshot captures the complete state of the review at that point in time, enabling historical verification and dispute resolution.

Supports filtering by snapshot type (created, modified, helpfulness_updated), date range queries, and cursor-based pagination for efficient retrieval of large audit histories.

Review authors can view all snapshots of their own reviews. Platform administrators can access snapshots of any review for dispute resolution and audit purposes. Snapshot data is immutable and cannot be deleted or modified.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_review_snapshots table filtering by ecommerce_mall_review_id matching the {reviewId} path parameter.

Apply optional search filters from the request body:
- snapshot_type filter: Limit to specific change types (created, modified, helpfulness_updated)
- date_range: Filter snapshots by created_at timestamp (created_at_gte, created_at_lte)
- ordering: Sort by created_at descending (newest first) or ascending
- pagination: cursor-based pagination with page_size, cursor parameters

Database query joins with ecommerce_mall_reviews if customer_id verification is needed for authorization checks.

Authorization:
- For customer actors: Verify the review belongs to the authenticated customer_id before returning snapshots
- For admin actors: No authorization restriction, access all snapshots
- For guest actors: Return empty list or unauthorized error

Return paginated results using IPageIEcommerceMallReviewSnapshot.ISummary structure with cursor-based pagination metadata including hasNextCursor for efficient next-page retrieval.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of review snapshot summaries

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of notifications filtered by actor type, read status, and other search criteria.

This operation provides advanced filtering capabilities for notification management. Users can filter by notification type (order updates, seller approvals, platform announcements, system alerts), read status (unread, read, acknowledged), and create date ranges. Full-text search on notification titles and bodies is supported for finding specific content.

The operation returns notification summaries optimized for list display, including the notification title, a truncated body preview, type classification, read status, and the display name of the actor who sent or is associated with the notification. Pagination is cursor-based for efficient handling of large result sets.

Security and access control are enforced based on actor type: customers can only view their own notifications, sellers can only view seller-specific notifications, while admins and super administrators have access to platform-wide notifications. Guest notifications are scoped to the current session.

The operation supports multiple sorting options including creation date, read timestamp, and title, with ascending or descending order. Results are paginated with configurable page sizes to optimize performance for list views.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_notifications table with polymorphic joins to recipient subtype tables.

Apply filters from requestBody:
- actor_type: Filter by recipient_type (customer, seller, admin, superAdmin, guest)
- actor_id: Filter by recipient_id matching the actor_id in subtype table
- read_status: Filter by read status (unread, read, acknowledged)
- type: Filter by notification type (order_update, seller_approval, platform_announcement, system_alert)
- created_at_from/to: Date range filtering
- search: Full-text search on title and body using PostgreSQL gin_trgm_ops index

Apply sorting:
- sort: 'created_at', 'read_at', 'title'
- order: 'asc', 'desc'

Apply pagination:
- page: Cursor-based pagination using created_at as cursor
- per_page: Maximum 100 items per page

Join logic:
- Main query on ecommerce_mall_notifications
- LEFT JOIN ecommerce_mall_notification_recipients ON notification_id
- LEFT JOIN polymorphic recipient tables based on actor_type
- Include actor display names where available (customer.display_name, seller.shop_name)

Business rules:
- Customers can only see their own notifications (actor_id = current customer.id)
- Sellers can only see their own notifications
- Admins and superAdmins can see all notifications
- Guest notifications are session-scoped

Return summary fields optimized for list display: id, title, body (truncated), type, status, created_at, read_status, actor_id, actor_display_name.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single notification by its unique identifier for administrator review.

This operation allows administrators to view the details of a specific notification in the system. Notifications contain important information such as order updates, seller approval status changes, platform announcements, and system alerts. Administrators use this operation to monitor system-wide communications and verify notification delivery status.

The notification title and body are displayed in the administrator's notification list and detail views. The status field indicates whether the notification has been read or remains unread. The type field categorizes the notification (e.g., 'order_update', 'seller_approval', 'platform_announcement', 'system_alert') for filtering and organizational purposes.

Only notifications that have not been soft-deleted are returned. Attempting to retrieve a soft-deleted notification will result in a not-found error. Administrators have full visibility into all notifications on the platform as they have platform-wide oversight capabilities. The operation retrieves notifications through the notification recipients system to ensure data integrity and audit trail compliance.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the ecommerce_mall_notifications table for a single record matching the provided notificationId UUID.

1. Validate that notificationId is a valid UUID format
2. Execute SELECT query with WHERE id = $1 AND deleted_at IS NULL
3. Check if notification exists and is not soft-deleted
4. Verify actor authorization - ensure the requesting actor has access to this notification via ecommerce_mall_notification_recipients junction table or actor-specific notification reference table (ecommerce_mall_notification_of_customers, ecommerce_mall_notification_of_sellers, ecommerce_mall_notification_of_admins, ecommerce_mall_notification_of_super_admins, ecommerce_mall_notification_of_guests)
5. Return notification object with all fields: id, title, body, type, status, created_at, updated_at
6. If notification not found or actor not authorized, return 404 Not Found
7. If actor lacks permission, return 403 Forbidden

Error handling:
- 404: Notification does not exist, has been soft-deleted, or actor has no access
- 403: Actor does not have permission to view this notification
- 400: Invalid notificationId format

responseBody.description: Full notification details including title, body content, type classification, and read status

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the notification to retrieve
parameters.name: notificationId

operations.description:
Create a new system notification for delivery to one or more actors across the platform.

This operation creates a notification message with a title, body content, and type category. The notification is then delivered to specified recipients, which can be customers, sellers, administrators, super administrators, or guests. Each recipient receives the notification through the polymorphic actor reference system, enabling the platform to track delivery status and read states per actor type.

Notifications support multiple recipients in a single creation operation. The platform automatically creates the necessary actor-specific reference records (notification_of_customers, notification_of_sellers, notification_of_admins, notification_of_super_admins, or notification_of_guests) based on the recipient types specified. Each delivery is tracked through the notification_recipients junction table with a read_status of 'unread'.

Customer, seller, and recipient delivery records support soft deletion (marked by deleted_at timestamp) to preserve audit trails. However, admin, super admin, and guest notification reference records do not support soft deletion and are permanently removed when deleted.

Valid notification types include: order_update, seller_approval, platform_announcement, system_alert, cancellation_decision, refund_decision, shipment_update. The notification status is automatically set to 'unread' upon creation and is updated to 'read' when the recipient views the notification.

The notification creation process is atomic - all recipient deliveries succeed together or none are created, maintaining data consistency across the notification system.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new notification record in ecommerce_mall_notifications table with the provided title, body, and type. Status is automatically set to 'unread'.

For each recipient specified in the request body:
1. Validate the actor exists and matches the specified actor_type
2. Create a record in the appropriate actor reference table:
   - notification_of_customers for customer recipients
   - notification_of_sellers for seller recipients
   - notification_of_admins for admin recipients
   - notification_of_super_admins for super admin recipients
   - notification_of_guests for guest recipients
3. Create a record in ecommerce_mall_notification_recipients with the notification_id, actor_type, actor_id, and read_status='unread'

Transaction requirements:
- All operations must complete within a single database transaction
- If any recipient validation fails, roll back all changes
- Ensure notification_id is properly linked to all actor references via 1:1 constraint

Validation rules:
- title: required, non-empty string, max length 255 characters
- body: required, non-empty string
- type: required, must match one of the allowed notification type values
- recipients: required, non-empty array with at least one recipient
- Each recipient must have valid actor_type and actor_id that exists in the database

Error handling:
- Return 400 Bad Request if validation fails
- Return 404 Not Found if any referenced actor does not exist
- Return 500 Internal Server Error if database transaction fails

responseBody.description: The created notification with assigned ID and timestamps

requestBody.description: Notification creation data including content and recipient information

Update an existing notification entity with new title and body content.

This operation modifies the notification record in the ecommerce_mall_notifications table, replacing the current title and body with the provided values. The notification's type and status fields remain unchanged unless explicitly included in the update payload, though note that the database schema enforces unique constraints on type and status columns, which may restrict certain updates.

**Security Considerations**:

Only platform administrators with appropriate privileges can modify system notifications. The operation validates that the notification exists and is not soft-deleted before applying updates.

**Related Operations**:

- `GET /notifications/{notificationId}` - Retrieve notification details before updating
- `PATCH /notifications` - Search/list notifications with filters
- `DELETE /notifications/{notificationId}` - Soft delete a notification

Return the updated notification record with all fields including the new updated_at timestamp.

operations.description:
Permanently removes a system notification from the ecommerceMall platform.

This operation deletes a notification record identified by its UUID, including all associated polymorphic actor references (customer, seller, admin, superAdmin, or guest) and notification recipient tracking data. The deletion follows the soft-delete pattern, marking records as deleted via the deleted_at timestamp rather than physically removing them from the database, preserving audit trail integrity.

**Administrative Access Required**: Only platform administrators can execute this operation to maintain system-wide notification management control. Regular actors (customers, sellers, guests) cannot delete notifications directed to them.

**Related Operations**: Notification delivery and status updates are managed through separate PATCH operations on notification_recipients to mark notifications as read or acknowledged.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Execute soft-delete on ecommerce_mall_notifications table by setting deleted_at to current timestamp (UTC).

Transaction workflow:
1. Validate notificationId exists in ecommerce_mall_notifications
2. Verify current actor has admin privileges
3. Begin database transaction
4. Mark notification as deleted: SET deleted_at = NOW() WHERE id = notificationId
5. Cascade delete all related records (handled by ON DELETE CASCADE constraints):
   - ecommerce_mall_notification_of_admins records
   - ecommerce_mall_notification_of_customers records
   - ecommerce_mall_notification_of_guests records
   - ecommerce_mall_notification_of_sellers records
   - ecommerce_mall_notification_of_super_admins records
   - ecommerce_mall_notification_recipients records
6. Commit transaction
7. Return success status

Error handling:
- 404 Not Found: notificationId does not exist
- 403 Forbidden: actor lacks admin privileges
- 409 Conflict: notification already deleted (deleted_at is not null)

No response body returned on successful deletion.

parameters.name: notificationId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of shipping addresses belonging to the authenticated customer.

This operation provides comprehensive address listing capabilities for the ecommerce_mall_addresses table. Customers can view all their saved shipping addresses from their account settings, including recipient name, recipient phone number, street address, city, state/province, default address status, and creation timestamp. The response includes pagination metadata to handle large address lists efficiently.

Addresses are filtered by the authenticated customer's ID, ensuring data isolation between customers. Customers can only retrieve their own addresses. Soft-deleted addresses (records with deleted_at set) are excluded from results to maintain data isolation and order history integrity. Only active addresses can be used for new orders.

The operation supports pagination with configurable page size and cursor-based navigation for efficient handling of large datasets. The default address (is_default = true) is clearly identified in each record for checkout convenience.

This endpoint is part of the shipping address management functionality, allowing customers to view their saved addresses before creating, editing, or deleting them. The list operation is typically used as a prerequisite for other address management operations such as GET /addresses/{id} or DELETE /addresses/{id}.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_addresses table with filters applied.

Filtering:
- Customer ID: Automatically filtered by authenticated user's ID (data ownership enforcement)
- Optional: Recipient name pattern match
- Optional: City or state prefix match
- Optional: Creation date range
- Optional: Address status (if supported)

Sorting:
- Default: Created at descending (newest first)
- Optional: Sort by recipient name (ascending/descending)
- Optional: Sort by city (ascending/descending)

Pagination:
- Cursor-based pagination using created_at timestamp or ID
- Configurable page size (default: 20, max: 100)
- Return next cursor for pagination continuation

Query optimization:
- Index on customer_id, created_at, recipient_name
- Avoid N+1 queries by joining efficiently
- Return summary fields only (no deep nested data)

Authorization:
- Requires customer authentication
- Verify address belongs to authenticated customer (enforce data isolation)

operations.description:
Create a new shipping address for the authenticated customer account.

This operation enables customers to add delivery locations to their account for use during order placement. Each address stores complete recipient information (name and phone number) and full street address details (street, city, state) required for shipping labels and delivery coordination.

The authenticated customer creates addresses associated with their account. All required address fields must be provided during creation: recipient_name, recipient_phone, street, city, and state. Addresses with missing required information are rejected with validation errors.

Upon successful creation, the new address is added to the customer's saved addresses list. If the customer has no existing saved addresses, this address is automatically designated as the default address for convenience during checkout. Otherwise, it is created as a non-default address that the customer can set as default through address editing.

Addresses are soft-deleted when removed, meaning they are marked as deleted rather than permanently removed from the database. This preserves address information in historical order records even after removal from the customer's active address list. New orders placed after an address update or deletion will use the current active address information.

**Authorization**: Only authenticated customers can create addresses. Guest users and unauthenticated visitors cannot access this endpoint.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Extract customer ID from authentication context (JWT token)
2. Validate request body contains all required fields:
   - recipient_name: non-empty string
   - recipient_phone: non-empty string (may include country code)
   - street: non-empty string (may include apartment/suite)
   - city: non-empty string
   - state: non-empty string
3. Check if customer has existing addresses (query ecommerce_mall_addresses where customer_id = authenticated customer)
4. If customer has no existing addresses, set is_default = true
5. If customer has existing addresses, set is_default = false
6. Insert new record into ecommerce_mall_addresses with:
   - id: auto-generated UUID
   - ecommerce_mall_customer_id: from authentication
   - recipient_name, recipient_phone, street, city, state: from request body
   - is_default: determined in step 4-5
   - created_at: current timestamp
   - updated_at: current timestamp
   - deleted_at: null (active address)
7. Return the created address record with all fields including generated id

requestBody.description: Shipping address information for the new delivery location.

Retrieve a single shipping address by its unique identifier.

The endpoint enforces data isolation by ensuring customers can only view their own addresses. Attempts to access another customer's address will result in a not found error for security and privacy protection.

Soft-deleted addresses are excluded from results to maintain data integrity and prevent access to removed addresses.

Related operations:
- PATCH /addresses - list all customer addresses with search and pagination
- POST /addresses - create a new shipping address
- PUT /addresses/{addressId} - update an existing address
- DELETE /addresses/{addressId} - remove a shipping address

Query ecommerce_mall_addresses table for the address matching the provided addressId UUID.

4. Verify the address is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null)

Error handling:

operations.description:
Remove a shipping address from your address book.

This operation permanently removes the address from your active address list by marking it as deleted. The address is soft-deleted, meaning the address data is preserved in the database for historical order records but no longer available for new orders or address selection.

**Address Requirements**:

- The address must belong to the authenticated customer making the request
- The address must not be associated with any pending or active orders
- If the address is marked as your default shipping address, you must ensure you have at least one other valid address in your address book

**Deletion Behavior**:

- The deleted_at timestamp is set to the current time, marking the address as deleted
- The address is removed from your address list and cannot be selected for new orders
- Historical order records retain the original address information at the time of purchase
- The deletion is permanent and the address cannot be recovered

**Associated Order Validation**:

- Addresses linked to orders in active states (waiting for shipping, shipped, cancelled awaiting refund) cannot be deleted
- Orders in completed states with no pending transactions do not prevent deletion
- The system checks all order associations before permitting deletion

**Default Address Handling**:

- Deleting your default address requires you to have an alternative address available
- The system will not automatically select a new default
- You must manually select another address as default through the address update operation

This operation is available to authenticated customers only. Unauthenticated users cannot delete addresses.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Validate customer authentication and extract customer_id from session token
2. Retrieve the address by addressId from ecommerce_mall_addresses where customer_id matches
3. Verify the address belongs to the authenticated customer
4. Check for associated orders in active states:
   - Query ecommerce_mall_orders joined with ecommerce_mall_addresses via customer association
   - Filter for orders where shipping address_id equals addressId
   - Check order status: if ANY order has status in ['waiting_for_shipping', 'shipped', 'cancelled'] with pending refund, return error
5. Check if address is marked as is_default = true
   - If true and this is the only address for customer, return error requiring at least one address
6. Set deleted_at to current timestamp in database transaction
7. Create snapshot in ecommerce_mall_address_snapshots before deletion (copy all current fields)
8. Commit transaction
9. Return 204 No Content (or 200 with null body)

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the shipping address to delete.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of system audit snapshots tracking point-in-time state changes across products, product variants, reviews, cancellation requests, and refund requests.

This operation provides advanced search capabilities including filtering by entity type (product, product_variant, review, cancellation_request, refund_request), entity ID, actor ID, date range, and version numbers. The response includes paginated snapshot summaries optimized for administrative oversight and dispute resolution contexts.

Sellers can view snapshots of their own products, variants, and reviews. Administrators and super administrators have full access to all snapshots across the platform. Snapshots are immutable audit records that preserve the complete state of entities at specific points in time.

Use this endpoint to reconstruct historical entity states, investigate disputes, verify when specific prices or product details were active, or maintain compliance audit trails.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query ecommerce_mall_snapshots table with pagination and filtering.

Apply search filters on:
- entity_type: filter by snapshot type ('product', 'product_variant', 'review', 'cancellation_request', 'refund_request')
- entity_id: filter by specific entity ID
- actor_id: filter by actor who made the change
- created_at range: filter by snapshot creation date range
- version: filter by specific version number
- ordering: sort by created_at (descending by default for latest first)

Apply access control based on actor role:
- Customer/Seller: only view snapshots where actor_id matches their ID or entity_id references their owned entities
- Administrator/SuperAdmin: view all snapshots without restrictions

Join with entity tables when needed to enrich response with entity metadata.

Return cursor-based pagination using created_at timestamps for efficient large result sets.

Include snapshot_data as JSON string containing the complete state at snapshot time.

operations.description:
Retrieves a specific snapshot record from the audit trail system.

This operation returns a single snapshot identified by its unique identifier. Snapshots capture the complete state of entities (products, variants, reviews, cancellation requests, and refund requests) at the moment of change, enabling historical state reconstruction for dispute resolution, audit compliance, and customer transparency.

The snapshot includes:

- Entity identification: entity_type and entity_id specifying what entity was modified
- Actor attribution: actor_id indicating who made the change (customer, seller, admin, or super_admin)
- Snapshot data: complete JSON representation of the entity state at that point in time
- Version tracking: sequential version number for chronological ordering
- Timestamps: created_at showing when the snapshot was recorded

Authorization:

- Customers can view snapshots related to their own actions (reviews they wrote, cancellation/refund requests they submitted)
- Sellers can view snapshots of their products, product variants, and cancellation/refund requests involving their orders
- Administrators can view all snapshots on the platform for oversight purposes

When a snapshot is retrieved, the snapshot_data field contains a complete JSON object representing the entity state. For product snapshots, this includes product name, description, category, base price, all images with their order, and all variants with their SKU codes, option values, prices, and stock quantities. For order item snapshots, the data preserves the product name, description, variant options, price, and seller shop name and logo as they existed at the time of purchase.

Important notes:

- Snapshots are immutable and cannot be modified or deleted once created
- Deleted products and their snapshots remain accessible for historical reference
- Multiple snapshots for the same entity can be compared by version number or timestamp to identify the sequence of changes
- The exact conditions at any point in time can be reconstructed from the snapshot_data

This operation is commonly used in:

- Customer order history pages to show what product details were displayed at purchase time
- Dispute resolution workflows to determine what state an entity was in when a transaction occurred
- Seller product management dashboards to review change history
- Administrator oversight tools to track platform activity and investigate issues
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
1. Validate snapshotId is a valid UUID format
2. Query ecommerce_mall_snapshots table where id = snapshotId
3. Verify access control:
   - If actor is customer: verify snapshot.actor_id matches authenticated customer ID, OR snapshot entity_type is review with review.customer_id matching authenticated customer ID, OR snapshot entity_type is cancellation_request/refund_request with request.customer_id matching authenticated customer ID
   - If actor is seller: verify snapshot relates to seller's products (entity_type=product with product.seller_id matching, or entity_type=product_variant with variant's product.seller_id matching, or order_item with order customer having seller's products)
   - If actor is admin: allow access to all snapshots
   - If actor is super_admin: allow access to all snapshots
4. Return snapshot record with all fields:
   - id: String UUID
   - actor_id: String? (nullable)
   - entity_id: String UUID
   - entity_type: String ('product', 'product_variant', 'review', 'cancellation_request', 'refund_request')
   - snapshot_data: String (JSON)
   - version: Int
   - created_at: DateTime
   - updated_at: DateTime
5. If snapshot not found, return 404 Not Found
6. If access denied, return 403 Forbidden

responseBody.description: Complete snapshot record with entity state at the time of change

operations.description:
Adds a product to a customer's wishlist for future purchase consideration.

This operation creates a new wishlist item entry that links the authenticated customer to a specific product. The system records which customer owns the wishlist item and which product is being saved, enabling customers to build a personal collection of products they want to remember for later purchase.

Wishlist items operate at the product level rather than variant level, providing flexibility when product variants change or new variants are added. The same product can appear in multiple customers' wishlists, but a customer cannot add the same product multiple times to their own wishlist.

**Security and Access Control**:
- Only authenticated customers can add items to their wishlist
- Customers can only view and manage their own wishlist items
- Products must be available on the platform to be added
- Duplicate additions are rejected (customer cannot add same product twice)

**Related Operations**:
- GET /customers/wishlist-items: Retrieve the customer's complete wishlist
- DELETE /customers/wishlist-items/{wishlistItemId}: Remove a product from the wishlist
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new wishlist item record in the ecommerce_mall_wishlist_items table.

**Implementation Steps:**
1. Extract customer_id from authenticated user session/claims
2. Validate product_id from request body exists in ecommerce_mall_products table
3. Check if product is available (not deleted/hidden) - use product status from schema
4. Verify no duplicate wishlist item exists for this customer-product combination using unique constraint [customer_id, product_id]
5. Insert new record with:
   - id: auto-generated UUID
   - customer_id: from authenticated user
   - product_id: from request body
   - created_at: current timestamp
   - updated_at: current timestamp
   - deleted_at: null
6. Return the created wishlist item with all fields

**Error Handling:**
- Return 400 Bad Request if product_id is missing or invalid UUID format
- Return 404 Not Found if product does not exist or is not available
- Return 409 Conflict if customer already has this product in their wishlist (duplicate unique constraint)
- Return 401 Unauthorized if customer is not authenticated

The endpoint provides read-only access to wishlist item data, allowing customers to view products they have marked for future purchase consideration.

The wishlist item serves as a saved product reference that customers can use to defer purchase decisions while maintaining a record of their interests. Each wishlist item is owned by a single customer and references a product from the catalog, enabling customers to build personalized collections of items they may want to purchase later.

Access to this endpoint is restricted to the customer who owns the wishlist item, ensuring data privacy and preventing unauthorized access to other customers' saved products. Customers can only view their own wishlist items, as confirmed by the authorization system which validates ownership before returning the wishlist item data.

The response includes product information such as product name, price, images, and variant details for display in the customer's wishlist. Pagination supports configurable page sizes with cursor-based navigation for efficient large result set handling.

Security ensures customers can only access their own wishlist items through authentication. Customers can manage their wishlist items through separate operations to add or remove products from their collections.
